# Acceptance

Spec #1's Testing Decisions list the Gateway-seam acceptance scenarios, from plan Phases 2 to 4. Each row names the tests that prove the scenario. A test name is `Class.Method`. Classes without a project prefix are in `tests/ModularMonolith.Tests`, which drives the Proving Sample through Module Gateways (and HTTP) against PostgreSQL in Testcontainers. The `PouryaKit.Cqrs.Tests` classes run the dispatcher with stand-ins and no database, and support a row that a Gateway-seam test already proves. Every scenario has Gateway-seam proof; a row notes any supplementary check that calls the dispatcher directly.

The plan row is the B.1 behaviour the Phase acceptance line cites, or the Phase when it cites none.

The Wave 2 sections without a `validate.py` PASS line (among them #37, #38, #44, #56, #57 and the #54 packages), and the PASS lines older than their section's last source change, are covered by the integrated runs: the close-out's final `validate.py` run on the `feat/wave-2` tip, which #54's closing comment cites, is the package record for all of them.

|---|---|---|---|
| A failed Result rolls back | 2 | `UnitOfWorkTests.A_failed_result_returned_after_writing_leaves_nothing_written`; `NotificationTests.An_operation_that_rolls_back_stores_no_notification` ("failed Result") | The second test also shows that no Outbox row is left. |

## Structure seam

The third seam of the Testing Decisions is proven in `tests/PouryaKit.ArchitectureTests`, described in [the architecture doc](architecture/README.md#structure-tests). Each rule judges the Proving Sample and an offending fixture Module (`tests/PouryaKit.ArchitectureTests/Offending`) with the same function.

| Rule | Proven by |
|---|---|
| No Module references another Module's implementation; Contracts reference nothing from the Kit | `ModuleBoundaryTests` |
| A Module's only public types are its Composition Root and what its Host implements for it | `ModuleBoundaryTests` |
| Feature code never saves, commits, writes in bulk or calls a step only the Kit runs | `FeatureCodeTests` |
| No transport type in Feature code; no envelope storage in a Module's DbContext | `FeatureCodeTests` |
| No application code implements a contract the Kit fills for its pipeline, the dispatcher and the two optional slots included | `PipelineContractTests` (ticket #54) |
| Only the Kit's drain clears Domain Events | `FeatureCodeTests` |
| Only Domain sets up JSON options; Web, Cqrs and Caching apply `UsePouryaKitJson`, and Messaging.Wolverine alone its strict variant `UsePouryaKitWireJson` | `SharedJsonTests` (tickets #34, #60) |
| No Dapper write to an aggregate's table | `DapperWriteTests` |
| Only Core lists the types of an assembly; every other Kit package asks `ImplementingTypes`, except `PouryaKit.Validation`, which finds its validators with FluentValidation's own assembly scanner on purpose ([its provenance record](provenance/PouryaKit.Validation.md)) | `TypeLookupTests` (ticket #55; the exception named by ticket #99) |
| Every Kit package's dependency closure matches plan section C | `PackageGraphTests` |
| No package with a licence outside the permissive list | `LicenceTests` |

## Stored-delivery schema regression

`StoredDeliveriesSchemaTests.Message_store_queries_use_the_exact_schema_name` exercises IDs, delivery enumeration, pending counts and deletion against PostgreSQL with `review-store` and `review-store"quoted`. These tests provision the message tables directly. They prove the reader quotes identifiers correctly; Wolverine 6.46.0 itself fails Host startup with these names in both Solo and Balanced mode, so this is not a Gateway or custom-schema Host-startup guarantee.

## Wave 2 shared JSON, ticket #34

Spec #33, user story 8: one JSON configuration for typed IDs, HTTP and message envelopes. `UsePouryaKitJson` in Domain is the configuration; Web and Messaging.Wolverine apply it.

| Acceptance | Proven by |
|---|---|
| A typed ID over Guid, long, int or string is written as its bare value and read back | `PouryaKit.Domain.Tests` `TypedIdTests.Ids_round_trip_through_json_as_their_bare_value`; `TypedIdTests.Ids_inside_an_object_are_written_as_their_bare_values_under_camel_case_names` |
| The configuration writes the same text from default options, Web-default options (applied twice) and options set to snake_case with the strict default encoder | `PouryaKit.Domain.Tests` `TypedIdTests.The_kits_json_options_write_the_same_text_from_default_web_or_snake_case_strict_options_and_when_applied_twice` |
| A typed ID has the same JSON in an HTTP response and in its delivered envelope, which reads back to the same ID | `SharedJsonTests.A_typed_id_is_written_the_same_in_an_http_response_and_in_its_delivered_envelope` |
| Guid typed IDs stay version 7 | `PouryaKit.Domain.Tests` `TypedIdTests.New_guid_ids_are_time_ordered` |
| One registration, in Domain; package references unchanged | `PouryaKit.ArchitectureTests` `SharedJsonTests`; `PackageGraphTests` |

The HTTP and envelope test compares `GET /catalog/products` (`ProductId` and `CategoryId`) with the stored envelopes of `ProductCreatedDomainEvent`, one per subscription, read from PostgreSQL in Testcontainers after delivery, and reads each back with the Host's own Wolverine serializer. With Wolverine's default options in place of `UsePouryaKitJson`, the envelope holds `{"value":"<guid>"}` and the test fails.

Packed API: the single-module clean consumer ([`scripts/packaging/consumers/single-module.cs`](../scripts/packaging/consumers/single-module.cs)) serializes a typed ID through `new JsonSerializerOptions().UsePouryaKitJson()` from the packed Domain. `python3 scripts/packaging/validate.py --no-fetch` on the fix-round source (commit `cf7d258`, before this paragraph was added) printed `PASS 13 packages, 15 clean consumers, negative controls and MinVer proof`, with the Release runtime suite at 391 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

## Phase 5 package proof, ticket #25

[`python3 scripts/packaging/validate.py`](../scripts/packaging/validate.py) runs the existing suite against one Release build, then packs with `--no-build`. Its evidence directory records runtime results separately from package and consumer results. [Package guidance](packages.md) gives the command, artifact contract and evidence limits.

| Acceptance | Proof |
|---|---|
| MinVer is shared, with minimum 0.1, v prefix and preview.0 default | Real package/build versions agree; `minver.json` records an isolated Git repository's untagged, tagged and post-tag outputs |
| Exactly the inventory's shipped packages, every entry of `inventory.json`; tests and samples excluded | Every project is evaluated against `inventory.json`; `InventoryTests.test_inventory_is_nonempty_and_exact` and `inventory-controls.log` reject empty/missing/extra/mismatched entries and accidental packability |
| MIT/notices, repository/source commit and SourceLink in each artifact | `PackageArtifactTests.Invalid_release_metadata_is_rejected`, `Embedded_source_link_identifies_the_commit_and_rejects_a_different_commit`, and the package validator inspect archive bytes and embedded PDBs |
| Existing graph and license restrictions survive shipping | `PackageGraphTests.Produced_nuspecs_obey_the_same_reference_rules_as_source_projects`, artifact graph checks and `consumer-closures.log` reuse `PackageGraph` and `LicenceTests` |
| Every package and supported composition restores/builds independently of Kit source | One package-only application per library package, every library entry of `inventory.json`, the single-Module set without Modularity/Messaging, and the copied modular monolith build with isolated caches, source mapping, exact versions and nupkg SHA-256 checks |
| Defects fail the shared path | Per-control logs show missing/extra artifacts, wrong version/commit, missing notices, forbidden references and invalid symbols rejected by the same package validator |

This is package restore/build proof, alongside the existing PostgreSQL runtime suite above. It proves neither hosted publication nor private-feed recovery.

## Phase 5 CI validation, ticket #26

[CI guidance](ci.md) defines the read-only reusable workflow, preserved artifact contract and trusted-main handoff. The shared path replaces the former source-only build/test job and retains the AI configuration check.

| Acceptance | Evidence and remaining gate |
|---|---|
| Build/test/pack/consumers share full-history Release output | Hosted [initial green](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/actions/runs/37448645751) and [repaired green](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/actions/runs/37449774763) ran the actual merge SHA with full history/tags and `--no-fetch`: 386 runtime tests passed, thirteen packages and fifteen clean consumers validated at MinVer `0.1.0-preview.0.8`. |
| Exact tested SHA and retained original artifacts | Downloaded artifacts `11404508475` and `11406765985` match all thirteen manifest checksums. Their receipts identify tested merge SHAs `b47372f2cc28feae58f2fb2f2f01f0cd98b825d8` and `165d1d82b559454bc2bc214d867aab72b4649ed4`, with distinct PR heads/base and bounded logs/assets without caches or configuration. |
| Failed validation stays failed and preserves diagnostics | [Run 37449281223](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/actions/runs/37449281223) tested merge SHA `49ff3f2cbd1900136745964bdeadaceb1aa496aa`: runtime passed, deliberate consumer `CS0103` failed the package step/job and whole CI. Artifact `11405776196` retains diagnostics and a failure receipt with no successful version/manifest pointer. |
| PR credentials and writes are isolated | All three runs' actual job setup logs show only `Contents: read` and `Metadata: read`; only AI setup and package validation ran. Checkout removed credentials; inspected YAML forwards no secrets. Main, tag/release census and fork settings compare unchanged. |
| Same-repository and fork execution | [Proof PR #30](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/pull/30) observed green/failure/repaired green and closed without merging. Real private fork execution remains unverified under the [owner exception](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/issues/26#issuecomment-6013184398); same-repository execution and static settings do not prove fork execution. |

The [CI evidence table](ci.md#hosted-proof-boundary) records all run identities and observed boundaries. Local script tests and workflow lint complement this hosted evidence. Publication remains outside this ticket and must verify a successful trusted main run at the exact selected SHA; a PR receipt alone cannot authorize it.

## Phase 5 private publication, ticket #27

The owner adjusted scope on 2026-10-06 to clean packaging, MinVer versioning and standard private NuGet publication. [Private publication guidance](private-packages.md) describes the active workflow; [ticket #27](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/issues/27) records actual hosted runs and consumer evidence.

| Active check | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| Exact successful trusted main run, attempt and SHA | The focused workflow check executes the real authorization script against accepted push/manual-main cases and rejected PR/fork/branch/SHA/attempt/failure/job cases. Actual run provenance is fetched read-only before the privileged job. |
| Original artifact, inventory and hashes | Official download uses the original run/attempt name and rejects digest mismatches. The focused check executes the artifact verification shell and rejects mismatched receipts, versions, missing inventory and changed package bytes. |
| One standard private publisher | Workflow lint and inspection check job-scoped package-write permission, the fixed feed and the literal publication group with cancellation disabled. Actual hosted serialization requires hosted evidence. |
| Private-feed availability | Successful [publication run 37466084084](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/actions/runs/37466084084) at main SHA `b234f4f` published the original `0.1.0-preview.0.13` packages and restored all thirteen with fresh caches and GitHub mapping. Its producer, [CI run 37465576160](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/actions/runs/37465576160), passed 386 runtime tests with zero failures or skips and validated thirteen packages and fifteen clean consumers. |
| Named preview/rc versions | Owner-created tags on current main followed by manual CI use MinVer's existing tag version through the same build/test/pack path. No automated tag, release or compatibility policy is claimed. |

The prior custom HTTP protocol, remote-byte verifier and preflight SDK machinery are removed. `--skip-duplicate` skips HTTP 409; it does not establish matching remote bytes. [Plan Phase 5](foundation-review.md#phase-5-packaging-and-releases) records the release automation outside this scope (since 2026-10-10, ticket #90, its one statement). The active Phase 5 scope is complete. The active pipeline does not satisfy all original #24 acceptance criteria. The successful [retry run 37465070135](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/actions/runs/37465070135) completed `.10` from original run `37456433718` and artifact `11408539884`, with Domain skipped on HTTP 409, twelve packages pushed and all thirteen restored with fresh caches. Preserve those original artifacts and the retry record; never replace or repack that version. This adds no remote raw-byte identity proof.

## Wave 2 unregistered permission declarations fail fast, ticket #56

Spec #33; owner decision of 2026-10-07 on the question #38 left open. No structure test: the check reads the handlers the Host registers, so a structure test over the Proving Sample would catch nothing it misses.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|

## Wave 2 continuation trust only from the Kit, ticket #57

[Ticket #57](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/issues/57) under spec #33 (owner decision 2026-10-07; ADR 0007's amendment of that date). Proven at the Gateway seam, as permissions are in #38.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A context that application code builds with any causation id is not trusted. A permission-protected command and query sent with it are refused `PermissionErrors.Denied` when the Actor lacks the permission, and nothing commits. | `SecurityTests.A_context_application_code_builds_with_a_causation_is_not_trusted_and_its_actor_is_checked` | The Stub Module's `StampNoteCommand` and `ReadStampLedgerQuery`. Goes red when the permission check reads `CausationId` again. |
| A context from `Continue()` on a context that never ran, or whose Operation has ended, is not trusted: a protected command and query sent with it are refused `PermissionErrors.Denied` | `SecurityTests.A_context_continued_outside_the_operation_that_ran_it_is_not_trusted` | Goes red when `Continue()` is always trusted, and when the check reads `CausationId` |
| `Continue()` inside a running authorized Operation is a trusted continuation (G.6). An Operation that declares no permission continues into a protected query, which its Actor holds no permission for, and the query is served. `Continue()` is not trusted inside the checks of a query nested in the Operation, nor from a task that outlives the Operation. | `SecurityTests.A_running_authorized_operation_continues_into_a_permission_protected_query_without_its_actor_being_checked_again`; `OperationContextTests.A_question_to_another_module_continues_the_asking_operations_context` | The Stub Module's `AskStampLedgerQuery`, and Catalog's product question as `CatalogProducts` asks it. Both go red when `Continue()` is never trusted. The first also goes red when the dispatcher no longer clears the context during nested checks, and when the context does not end with the Operation. |
| A delivery restored from the Kit's Outbox headers stays trusted, and an application authorizer still runs for it with the original Actor | `SecurityTests.A_continuation_runs_a_permission_protected_command_on_its_recorded_authority_without_authorizing_the_actor_again`; `SecurityTests.An_application_authorizer_still_runs_for_a_continued_command_with_the_original_actor_and_can_refuse_it` | From #38. The second test now asserts `IsTrustedContinuation`. Both go red when the delivery step restores the context with the public constructor. |
| Cqrs's `InternalsVisibleTo` lists exactly `PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine` and `PouryaKit.Web`, and neither calls an internal member of Cqrs other than `OperationContext.RestoreTrusted` | `TrustedRestoreTests.Cqrs_opens_its_internals_to_kit_delivery_and_web_only`; `TrustedRestoreTests.The_packages_cqrs_opens_to_use_no_internal_member_of_it_but_the_trusted_restore` | Structure test, read from the attribute list and the IL. It catches a third assembly being added to the list, and an opened package using another internal member, which no runtime test sees. There is no `Offending/` case: an assembly outside the list cannot compile a call to an internal member. The tests went red with `PouryaKit.Security` added to the list, and with Messaging.Wolverine reading `Operation.Context` (internal at the time; public since #47). |

## Wave 2 Integration Event versioning, ticket #49

Spec #33, user stories 43 and 44. A wire name is one version of one contract type: Catalog publishes `ProductCreatedV1` (`catalog.product-created.v1`) and `ProductCreatedV2` (`catalog.product-created.v2`) from one Notification Handler during the transition; Inventory and Billing keep their v1 subscriptions, and Inventory's `inventory.product-categories` subscribes to v2 only. Nothing converts one version into another.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| One Operation publishes both versions, and each subscription applies only the version it declared, with its Receipt in the commit of its effect | `IntegrationEventVersionTests.One_operation_publishes_both_versions_and_each_subscription_applies_only_its_own_with_its_receipt_in_one_commit` | Against PostgreSQL: v1 envelopes only on `local://billing.product-created/` and `local://inventory.product-created/`, v2 only on `local://inventory.product-categories/`, no dead letter; one publication record per version; each effect carries the creating Actor, and its commit timestamp equals its subscription's Receipt's, both keyed by the one Domain Event identity. Goes red when every subscription is also routed the other version, and when Integration Event Receipts are keyed by Module instead of subscription. |
| A second type claiming a wire name, or one type under two wire names, is refused before the Host starts | `IntegrationEventWiringTests.A_composition_root_fails_on` ("a wire name twice", "a Domain Event's wire name", "one type under two wire names"); `IntegrationEventTests.Building_fails_when_another_host_of_the_process_already_sends_the_type_under_another_wire_name` | Refused by the declaration in the Composition Root, naming both types or both names; goes red with each check removed. |
| A type Wolverine would also route to another type's subscriptions fails the Host when it is built | `IntegrationEventVersionTests.Building_fails_when_wolverine_would_route_one_message_type_to_the_subscriptions_of_another` | Wolverine 6.46.0 routes a subscribed type to every message whose wire name, name or full name equals the type's full name, ignoring case. With the check removed, a v2 published under the v1 contract's full name was routed to `local://tests.routed/`, the v1 subscription's queue. |

Package proof: `python3 scripts/packaging/validate.py --no-fetch` on commit `d4eeb61` printed `PASS 15 packages, 17 clean consumers, negative controls and MinVer proof` at version `0.1.0-preview.0.29`, with its runtime suite at 421 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Its copied Proving Sample consumer carries the v2 declarations. No public signature of `PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine` changed; only `Publish`'s documentation did.

## Wave 2 Operation observability and local delivery traces, ticket #47

Spec #33, its observability decision, and [ADR 0009](adr/0009-w3c-trace-context-through-the-outbox.md), item 3. The chain is Catalog's `CreateProduct`, then the delivery of its Notification `catalog.product-created.publish-product-created`, which publishes `ProductCreatedV1`, then Inventory's `inventory.product-created`, through durable local queues against PostgreSQL. The tests use listeners only, with no exporter or telemetry backend. The proof is local: cross-process propagation over RabbitMQ is #52's.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A product created in Catalog and stocked in Inventory is one trace. `CreateProduct`'s Operation activity is a child of the upstream request, the publishing delivery's Operation a child of `CreateProduct`'s, and Inventory's delivery Operation a child of the publishing one: directly when only the Kit's source is listened, through Wolverine's execution span when `Wolverine` is sampled too. Each carries the upstream tracestate, and the product and its stock item are committed. | `ObservabilityTests.A_product_created_in_catalog_and_stocked_in_inventory_is_one_trace_with_the_upstream_tracestate` (both listener configurations) | Red when the Operation activity ends before the Unit of Work writes the Outbox, so the stored `parent-id` no longer names it. Red when the Outbox drops the tracestate header. Red, with only the Kit's source listened, when the delivery ignores the restored parent and every hop starts a new trace. |
| A stored retry, read back from the message store, stays in the publishing trace as a sibling of the failed attempt, with the tracestate, and the effect commits once | `ObservabilityTests.A_stored_retry_of_a_delivery_stays_in_the_publishing_trace_with_its_tracestate` | `DeliveryProbes.FailOnceAfterReceipt` fails the first attempt inside its transaction. Red when the header is dropped and when the fallback is removed. |
| Each command and query is one activity tagged with its Module, type, Actor kind and outcome (`success`, `failure` for a failed Result, `exception`), with its `ActivityStatusCode` and the Error codes or exception type. A nested command is a child of the one that sent it. Each has a duration measurement in fractional seconds with the same tags, an exception included. | `ObservabilityTests.Each_command_and_query_is_an_activity_and_a_fractional_duration_tagged_with_its_outcome` | The Stub Module's commands and query, through its Gateway. Red when the duration is recorded in whole seconds. |

## Wave 2 RabbitMQ transport, ticket #51

Spec #33, user story 45, its RabbitMQ decision and Testing Decision "Run real RabbitMQ and PostgreSQL with separate producer/consumer Hosts", on the topology of ADR 0006's #50 amendment, each row of its invariants table. `RabbitMqDeliveryTests` runs the Proving Sample's service composition: `ModularMonolith.Host` with the connection string `broker`, which hosts Catalog and Billing under the service name `modular-monolith`, and `Inventory.Host`, the unchanged Inventory Module under `inventory`, plus the tests' own second subscription `inventory.audit-product` to `ProductCreatedV1` and `DeliveryProbes`. Each is a real `IHost` from the sample's own composition, on a database of its own, joined only by RabbitMQ 4.3.6 (`Testcontainers.RabbitMq`, a vhost per test) and PostgreSQL 18.6 in Testcontainers. The tests live in `tests/ModularMonolith.Tests`, beside `AppFixture` but with their own `BrokerFixture`, because Catalog's commands are visible to that project only and the tests reuse its `DeliveryProbes`, `TestIssuer` and `AppFixture.ComposeHost`. Each "red" note names the behaviour switched off in a scratch run that failed the test.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A publication whose only subscription is in another Host is written to the Outbox in the commit that published it, and applied there once, its effect and Receipt in one commit; the publishing Host never receives its own publications back from the broker | `RabbitMqDeliveryTests.A_publication_whose_only_subscription_is_in_another_host_is_written_in_its_commit_and_applied_there_once` | `ProductCreatedV2`, whose only subscription is in `Inventory.Host`: held after the commit of the Notification Handler's delivery that published it, its outgoing row to `rabbitmq://exchange/catalog.product-created.v2` has the commit timestamp of the publication record. Red without the exchange route from the publication, and with the Host's queue bound to the wire names it publishes. |
| Two subscriptions of the receiving Host to one wire name: the failing one, whose handler writes its effect and returns a failed Result, is retried with the stored retry, leaves neither its effect nor its Receipt, is dead-lettered at `local://{subscription}/`, and once healed its replay commits one effect with its Receipt; the other commits its effect and Receipt once, without waiting for it | `RabbitMqDeliveryTests.A_failing_subscription_in_the_other_host_rolls_back_its_effect_is_dead_lettered_alone_and_its_replay_applies_once` | The tests' audit subscription writes `tests.product_audits` in Inventory's Unit of Work; it is held after its Receipt while the stock item commits, then fails three times with `IntegrationEventHandlerFailedException` (review finding F3). Red with the fan-out replaced by delivering every subscription in-line in the broker envelope, and with a failed delivery's transaction committed instead of rolled back. |
| A Host killed between storing the copies and marking the broker envelope handled fans it out again after it restarts, and each effect is applied once | `RabbitMqDeliveryTests.A_host_killed_between_storing_the_copies_and_marking_the_broker_envelope_handled_fans_out_again_and_applies_each_effect_once` | A trigger makes the broker rows' handled mark wait on an advisory lock the test holds; all four copies commit while the three broker rows are not handled; the Host is stopped as a kill leaves it (`StopMode.Quick`), the waiting backend terminated, and a new Host started: three broker rows handled, eight copies, one Receipt and effect each. This tests the order ADR 0006's #50 amendment read but did not test: Wolverine stores the copies before it marks the envelope handled. Red with the Receipt's result ignored. |
| A copy the receiving Host's store refuses fails its broker envelope, which is never marked handled: it is retried and dead-lettered in the store at `rabbitmq://queue/inventory`, and once the store is healed its replay fans it out again and each subscription applies it once with its Receipt | `RabbitMqDeliveryTests.A_copy_the_store_refuses_leaves_the_broker_envelope_unhandled_dead_lettered_at_the_host_queue_and_its_replay_applies_each_effect_once` | Review finding F6. A trigger on `wolverine.wolverine_incoming_envelopes` makes PostgreSQL refuse every insert of the audit's copy: while it stands, no audit copy and no audit Receipt, and the broker envelope is a dead letter whose exception is `Npgsql.PostgresException`; once the trigger is dropped and the dead letter replayed, one handled audit copy, one audit with its Receipt and one stock item. Red with the copies sent from the handler's own context, whose flush drops a copy the store refuses and marks the broker envelope handled. |

The copy is sent with `EndpointFor` through a bus enlisted in no transaction, and its durable local queue stores it as an incoming delivery owned by the node before the fan-out returns. Red when local queues keep what they receive in memory only. |

Red with the copies published through the type's routes, which include its exchange. |
| A retry waiting in the receiving Host survives its kill and restart, and a publication made while it is down waits in its queue and is delivered after it starts | `RabbitMqDeliveryTests.A_retry_waiting_in_the_other_host_survives_its_kill_and_a_publication_made_while_it_is_down_arrives_after_it_starts` | The waiting audit is a `Scheduled` row at `local://inventory.audit-product/`; three messages wait in the queue `inventory`. ## Wave 2 query caching and commit-aware invalidation, ticket #43

Spec #33, user stories 29 to 34, its caching decision, and the [ADR 0002](adr/0002-no-mediator-dependency.md) amendment for the second optional pipeline slot. The Proving Sample caches Catalog's `GetProduct`, which `RenameProduct` and `RemoveProducts` invalidate. A product renamed with plain SQL behind the cache's back tells a stored answer, the old name, from a read of the database, the new one; the Stub Module's cacheable queries record each run of their handler.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| An entry answers only the Actor and tenant that stored it: another person, a system Actor with the same id, and two tenants of one Actor each read their own | `CachingTests.An_entry_answers_only_its_own_actor_and_tenant` | Red when the Actor's id, its kind or the tenant is left out of the key. |
| A failed Result is never stored: a product created after a `NotFound` is found by the next query | `CachingTests.A_failed_result_is_never_stored` | Red when the failure is stored and returned on the next read. |
| Two concurrent identical queries in one Host run the handler once: the second joins the held first run, seen as `HybridCache`'s `StampedeJoin` event | `CachingTests.Two_concurrent_identical_queries_in_one_host_run_the_handler_once` | Red with a get-then-set in place of one `GetOrCreateAsync`. Single flight across Hosts is not claimed. |
| A committed rename evicts every Actor's warm entry, and a warm read answers the new name | `CachingTests.A_committed_rename_evicts_every_actors_entry_and_a_warm_read_answers_the_new_name` | Red when the dispatcher evicts nothing and when `RenameProduct` declares no tag. |
| After a committed removal, a warm read is `NotFound` for every Actor | `CachingTests.After_a_committed_removal_a_warm_read_is_not_found_for_every_actor` | `RemoveProducts` removes by name, so it declares `products`, a tag every `GetProduct` entry carries. Red when it declares no tag. |
| A rolled-back rename, refused at the save with `NameInUse`, evicts nothing: the valid entry survives | `CachingTests.A_rolled_back_rename_evicts_nothing_so_the_valid_entry_survives` | Red when the tags are evicted whatever the outcome. |
| A query nested in a write Unit of Work that rolls back leaves no entry: it saw the uncommitted tally inside, and runs again outside | `CachingTests.A_query_nested_in_a_write_unit_of_work_that_rolls_back_leaves_no_entry` | Red when a query inside an active Unit of Work goes through the cache. |
| A cached query's handler runs inside its Operation, so a continuation it creates is trusted | `CachingTests.A_cached_querys_handler_runs_inside_its_operation_so_a_continuation_it_creates_is_trusted` | Red when the slot passes the caller's token to `GetOrCreateAsync`, which makes `HybridCache` run the handler on the thread pool without the caller's `ExecutionContext`. |

| A query whose answer changes tracked state when serialized, a deferred enumerable that renames the folder it read, stores nothing: the starting caller and its joiner both receive the read-only check's `InvalidOperationException`, and a later read runs the handler again (re-review finding F6) | `CachingTests.A_query_whose_answer_changes_tracked_state_when_serialized_stores_nothing_and_its_joiner_receives_the_failure` | Red, with the success stored and no exception, when the read ends before the answer is serialized. |

## Wave 2 idempotency key retention, ticket #42 follow-up

The owner's decisions of 2026-10-07 on #42: a configurable retention for idempotency keys with asynchronous, batched cleanup outside the request path, and the context's identity rules in [ADR 0007](adr/0007-operation-context-set-by-the-scope-opener.md#amendment-2026-10-07-ticket-42-follow-up-the-context-in-the-idempotency-key). Each test starts a Host of the application whose `TimeProvider` is the test clock, so the store stamps a key with the test's time and the cleanup ticks when the test advances the clock; `CountNoteCommand` answers a number no other run answers, so a replay tells itself apart from a new run.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A key replays for its whole retention, 24 hours by default: one reserved 23 h 59 min before a cleanup replays after it, while the cleanup removes one reserved earlier, whose request id then runs as a new request. A key records the Host `TimeProvider`'s time it was reserved | `IdempotencyRetentionTests.A_key_replays_for_its_whole_retention_and_once_a_cleanup_removed_it_its_request_runs_as_a_new_one` | Red when the cutoff ignores the retention (the younger key is removed and runs again), and when the store stamps the system clock (no key expires on the test clock). |
| One cleanup removes more expired keys than a batch holds, `BatchSize` keys per statement until a batch is short | `IdempotencyRetentionTests.A_cleanup_removes_more_expired_keys_than_one_batch_in_batches_of_the_configured_size` | Five keys with `BatchSize` 2: three statements, as `IdempotencyKeysRemoved` logs. Red with one batch per tick, and without the `limit`. |
| A failed cleanup is logged and the next one removes the expired keys; the Host keeps running | `IdempotencyRetentionTests.A_failed_cleanup_is_logged_and_the_next_one_removes_the_expired_keys` | The `reserved_at` column is renamed for one tick. Red when the failure escapes the tick, which stops the Host. |
| `Retention = Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` keeps every key, and no cleanup runs | `IdempotencyRetentionTests.A_host_whose_retention_is_infinite_keeps_every_key` | Thirty days on the test clock, then a second of real time. Red when the cleanup runs anyway. |
| A Host with a retention, interval or batch size out of range fails to start, naming each: a retention that is not positive or exceeds 36500 days, an interval outside `PeriodicTimer`'s 1 ms to `uint.MaxValue - 1` ms, a batch size under 1 | `IdempotencyRetentionTests.A_host_whose_retention_interval_or_batch_size_is_out_of_range_fails_to_start_naming_each` (zero, -1 h and 0; 36501 days and 0.1 ms; a 50-day interval) | Review fix F2. Red without the options check, and without each bound: the 50-day interval then fails the start with `PeriodicTimer`'s own exception. |
| A repeat whose expired key a cleanup removes after its insert found the key held, and before it read the recorded success, runs as a new request and leaves one key | `IdempotencyRetentionTests.A_repeat_whose_expired_key_a_cleanup_removes_between_its_reservation_and_its_read_runs_as_a_new_request` | Review fix F3. An EF Core command interceptor on the Stub's DbContext advances the test clock right after that insert and waits until the cleanup removed the key. Red with one reservation attempt: the repeat throws. |
| A key table created before `CreateIdempotencyTable` added `reserved_at` fails the Operation with an `InvalidOperationException` that names the column and the SQL that adds it, and commits nothing | `IdempotencyRetentionTests.A_key_table_without_reserved_at_fails_the_operation_naming_the_column_and_its_fix` | Review fix F1: the column is renamed for the test. Red without the mapping of SQLSTATE 42703. No forward migration: the earlier shape never shipped, so only a local database migrated from an earlier Wave 2 build has it. |
| #42's guarantees hold with the timestamp and the shared null-tenant sentinel | `IdempotencyTests`; `PouryaKit.Cqrs.Tests.IdempotencyTests` | `IdempotencyTable.NoTenant` is now an alias of `OperationContext.NoTenant`. |
| `PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore` references `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions` | `PouryaKit.ArchitectureTests.PackageGraphTests` | Its section C row, under the standing rule for MIT `Microsoft.Extensions.*` packages. |
| The packed API compiles in a clean consumer | `scripts/packaging/consumers/PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore.cs` | Sets every `PouryaKitIdempotencyOptions` property. |
| Packages | No package added or bumped | `PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore` gains `PouryaKitIdempotencyOptions` and the direct reference `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions` 10.0.12 (MIT), the version `Directory.Packages.props` already pins; `CreateIdempotencyTable` adds the `reserved_at` column and its index, so the sample's and the Stub's `IdempotencyKeys` migrations create them. |

The package-only consumer of Persistence.EFCore built `PouryaKitIdempotencyOptions` from `consumers/PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore.cs` against the packed packages only, and the `modular-monolith` composition built the sample, whose `IdempotencyKeys` migration now creates `reserved_at`, from packages.

## Wave 2 cross-process tracing and standard Host recipes, ticket #52

Spec #33, its observability, outgoing-retry and template decisions, and [ADR 0009](adr/0009-w3c-trace-context-through-the-outbox.md)'s #52 amendment. The broker path was probed first, at `8b7ab96` before any change: `parent-id` and `pouryakit-tracestate` crossed RabbitMQ, and the receiving Host's fan-out copies named no parent unless Wolverine's source was sampled, so Inventory's delivery started a new trace (the amendment's table). `CrossProcessTracingTests` runs `ModularMonolith.Host` with a broker and `Inventory.Host`, each on its own database and joined only by RabbitMQ in Testcontainers, both in the test process, because an `ActivityListener` sees its own process only. The recipes are template content in `samples/ModularMonolith/src/ModularMonolith.ServiceDefaults`, not a Kit package; `Inventory.Host` composes them. No telemetry backend: listeners, and an exporter the test adds.

|---|---|---|
| A product created in the Catalog Host and stocked by `Inventory.Host` over RabbitMQ is one trace: Inventory's delivery Operation has the upstream trace id and tracestate, and its parent is the publishing Operation in the Catalog Host, or, with `Wolverine` sampled, Wolverine's span of the copy, whose parent is Wolverine's span of the broker envelope, whose parent is the publishing Operation; on the first attempt and on a stored retry | `CrossProcessTracingTests.A_product_created_in_the_catalog_host_and_stocked_by_inventory_host_is_one_trace_with_the_upstream_tracestate` (both listener configurations) | Red, with only the Kit's source listened, without the fan-out's `pouryakit-traceparent` write and without the delivery's fallback read; the Wolverine-sampled row stays green by design. Red in both without `pouryakit-tracestate` among the copied headers, and without `AddPouryaKitObservability()` in `Inventory.Host`. |
| `Inventory.Host`'s deliveries reach exporters added to the service defaults' own tracer and meter providers: the `pouryakit.operation` activity of the delivery and a `pouryakit.operation.duration` point tagged `InventoryModule`, `Deliver`, `success` | `HostRecipeTests.Inventory_hosts_deliveries_reach_the_exporters_of_its_service_defaults` | `SimpleActivityExportProcessor` and `BaseExportingMetricReader` over the test's own `BaseExporter`s, `MeterProvider.ForceFlush()` once the message store settled, since the rows commit before the Operation records its duration and ends its activity (review finding F2; with the delivery held 2 s after its commit, red waiting for the rows only, green waiting for the store). ## Wave 2 code generation for production, ticket #58

Spec #33, the owner's decision of 2026-10-07 that this is built in Wave 2, and [ADR 0004](adr/0004-commit-through-wolverine-ef-outbox.md)'s #58 amendment, following Wolverine's code generation guide for the pinned 6.46.0 (`JasperFx/wolverine` commit `dc63f46`, `docs/guide/codegen.md`) and its sample (`JasperFx/CritterStackSamples` commit `76ce8e2`, `CqrsMinimalApi/`). The early probe ran on the sample Host before the rest was built: `dotnet run -- codegen write` wrote `Internal/Generated/WolverineHandlers/GeneratedHandlerRegistry.cs` alone, an empty registry, and `dotnet run -- describe` named `PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine` as Wolverine's application assembly, the one Static mode loads generated types from; the Kit now sets it to the entry assembly. Built in Release without the compiler and started in Production against PostgreSQL, the sample Host then logged "Static with pre-generated types being loaded from ModularMonolith.Host" and Wolverine's missing-registry warning, built its message storage and started.

## Wave 2 template names as typed, ticket #59

Spec #33 and the owner's decision of 2026-10-07 that a name a namespace cannot hold is fixed, not documented (#53's fix round had documented it). The reference is Aspire's `aspire-starter` 13.6.1 (`microsoft/aspire` commit `3751e615`, `Aspire.ProjectTemplates`): generated with `-n acme-shop`, it names the folder `acme-shop.ApiService`, references `..\acme-shop.ApiService\acme-shop.ApiService.csproj` and writes `namespace acme_shop.Web`, because its source name `Aspire-StarterApplication.1` has a form as typed and a namespace-safe form that differ. The Kit keeps its `sourceName` and gets the same outcome with a `derived` symbol (dotnet templating wiki, "Reference for template.json").

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A generated solution restores and builds for `-n acme-shop`, `Acme.Shop`, `acme_shop` and `My Shop`: folders, files and the paths the solution and project references name carry the name as typed, the code its namespace-safe form, and the broker queue the derived service name | The four-name probe below, both templates from the produced package; `validate.py`, `template-monolith` generated with `-n Acme.Shop` and `template-modular-monolith` with `-n acme-shop`, each restored, built, smoke-tested and published | Before the fix, on a pack of `7bce996`'s templates, `-n acme-shop` generated `src/acme-shop.Host/` while the solution named `src/acme_shop.Host/acme_shop.Host.csproj`, and `dotnet restore` failed with `MSB3202` ("The project file … `acme_shop.Host.csproj` was not found") for the Host, the service defaults and the tests. |
| The template's own solution and project files name each project's path through the token `PouryaKitAppName` of the `projectName` symbol (`derived`, `valueSource` `name`, the `identity` form), never through the `sourceName`, and name only projects the template generates; the symbol is the same in both templates, and its token holds no form of the `sourceName` | `TemplateTests.Each_template_names_its_projects_paths_through_the_name_as_typed_the_same_way_in_both` | Negative cases: the old `src/ModularMonolith.Host/ModularMonolith.Host.csproj` line in the solution, and a project reference through the token to a project the template does not generate. Red once with the monolith solution's Host line put back to the old one. The packed sample files keep `ModularMonolith` for their namespaces. |
| The template's restore post-action restores the solution under its new name | The four-name probe: each name generated without `--no-restore` | The `primaryOutputs` path `ModularMonolith.slnx` is renamed with the files, so `-n acme-shop` restores `acme-shop.slnx`. |
| Out of scope | | The `sourceName` and the Proving Sample, unchanged; a `-n` validation (the engine has none). The generated project files set no `RootNamespace`, so MSBuild's default, the project's name with spaces as underscores (`acme-shop.Tests`), stays; all four names build with it. |

## Wave 2 strict wire reading, reserved broker names and messaging terms, ticket #60

Spec #33 and the owner's decisions of 2026-10-07 on RabbitMQ naming and routing: the verified topology stays, wire payloads are read strictly (option (a)), unknown members are decided with evidence, the `amq.` prefix is refused, service-name uniqueness is a deployment rule, and three messaging terms join the Glossary. The reference baseline is .NET 10 System.Text.Json's own options (`RespectRequiredConstructorParameters`, `RespectNullableAnnotations`, `JsonUnmappedMemberHandling`) through Wolverine 6.46.0's `UseSystemTextJsonForSerialization`; ADR 0006's #60 amendment records the decisions, the decompiled dead-letter path and the trade-off.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A received envelope whose body lacks a member its contract requires, or carries null for a non-nullable one, is never handled: it is dead-lettered at the receiving Host's broker queue with the `JsonException` naming the member, and no subscription receives a copy | `StrictWireReadingTests.A_body_without_a_member_its_contract_requires_or_with_null_for_one_is_dead_lettered_at_the_host_queue_with_the_error_and_never_handled`, two cases, two Hosts on RabbitMQ 4.3.6 and PostgreSQL 18.6: the Catalog Host publishes a contract of another shape under the wire name `Inventory.Host` receives | Red once with Wolverine reading through `UsePouryaKitJson`: both cases ran the handler with a null name. |
| A member the body carries and the receiving contract lacks is skipped, and the handler gets the members it has (the decision: skip, not `Disallow`) | `StrictWireReadingTests.A_body_with_a_member_its_contract_lacks_is_handled_with_the_members_it_has` | Red once with `JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow`: the envelope was dead-lettered and never applied. |
| HTTP bodies keep the lenient reading: a member a request body lacks binds as its default and the validator answers it | `WebTests.A_body_without_a_member_binds_it_as_its_default_and_validation_answers_400_for_it`; `PouryaKit.ArchitectureTests` `SharedJsonTests.Only_messaging_wolverine_reads_strictly_and_web_cqrs_and_caching_keep_the_lenient_reading` | Red once with Web applying `UsePouryaKitWireJson`: binding refused the body, a 400 without the validator's errors, and the structure test listed Web as a strict reader. No earlier Web test sent a body the strict reading would refuse. |
| A wire name, subscription name or service name beginning with `amq.`, in any case, is refused at registration with the rule in the message: `Publish`, `Receive`, `Subscribe` and `UsePouryaKitRabbitMq` | `IntegrationEventWiringTests.A_composition_root_fails_on` (three cases); `IntegrationEventWiringTests.A_service_name_rabbitmq_reserves_is_refused_when_the_host_joins_the_broker` | Red once with the prefix allowed (four failed) and with a case-sensitive check (the capitals case failed). A probe against RabbitMQ 4.3.6 refused the queue `amq.inventory` and the exchange `amq.product-created.v1` with 403 `ACCESS_REFUSED` ("contains reserved prefix 'amq.*'") and declared `AMQ.inventory`; the Kit refuses every case because it compares names ignoring case. No sample, template or test name begins with it. |
| Writing a null into a non-nullable member under the strict options fails with `JsonException` | `PouryaKit.Domain.Tests` `WireJsonTests.The_wire_options_refuse_to_write_null_into_a_non_nullable_member` (review finding F1) | Red once with `RespectNullableAnnotations` off: the null was written. That the failure lands in the Unit of Work's commit, where Wolverine's EF Core outbox serializes the envelope, is read from the decompiled outbox, not tested. |
| Terms | `GLOSSARY.md`: Wire name, Subscription, Service name; the Kit skill's terms line | |
| Out of scope | | The verified topology, the `serviceName` parameter, a contract-identity header and a schema registry (option (b), not recommended). Service-name uniqueness has no check: a replica and a foreign Host are indistinguishable on the broker. |

`python3 scripts/packaging/validate.py --no-fetch` on the ticket's source (commit `9b5922a`, before this paragraph was added) printed `PASS 21 packages, 24 clean consumers (2 generated from templates, smoke tests passed: template-monolith (-n Acme.Shop) 4, template-modular-monolith (-n acme-shop) 5), negative controls and MinVer proof` at version `0.1.0-preview.0.91`, with the Release runtime suite at 732 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. A first run on the same commit failed one runtime test, `CachingTests.With_redis_a_second_host_reads_the_entry_the_first_stored_without_running_its_handler`, whose own connection to its Redis container was refused (`RedisConnectionException` in `WaitUntilStoredAsync`); the rerun passed it unchanged, and it passed in both full Debug runs of the ticket.

On the merge of `feat/wave-2` at `29cf516` (#61) into the ticket's branch, `python3 scripts/packaging/validate.py --no-fetch` on the merge commit (`6528359`, before this paragraph was added) printed `PASS 21 packages, 24 clean consumers (2 generated from templates, smoke tests passed: template-monolith (-n Acme.Shop) 4, template-modular-monolith (-n acme-shop) 5), negative controls and MinVer proof` at version `0.1.0-preview.0.93`, with the Release runtime suite at 742 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. ## Wave 2 Module seam and composition checks, ticket #61

Spec #33, the owner's decisions of 2026-10-07 (A: a Module's Features live in its definition's assembly, inferred, with
named assemblies as the override, [ADR 0001](adr/0001-one-host-container.md)'s #61 amendment; B: a cacheable query is
never silent, [ADR 0002](adr/0002-no-mediator-dependency.md)'s #61 amendment) and the design-stage Codex review of the
Kit API cleanup, whose six findings the ticket's brief carries. The plan's own sketch is the reference: section D's
`module.Publish<ProductRenamedV1>("…")` with no Module argument ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-independent-delivery-through-a-routed-queue-per-subscription.md)'s #61 amendment).

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A publication, Snapshot, subscription, Notification Handler, delayed or recurring command declared without its Module in a Host of Modules fails the Host when it is built, naming the declaration, its form on the Module's builder and its form that names the Module | `CompositionCheckTests.A_module_declaration_made_without_its_module_in_a_host_of_modules_fails_the_host_when_built`, one case per declaration whose Module parameter #61 removed | Each declared on `builder.Services` of the Proving Sample's Host with the Stub Module; red once each with the check switched off: the Host then built. Before #61 such a declaration failed only at its first use, in the publisher, the Snapshot step, the delivery's Unit of Work router or the delayed-command scheduler (the removed Snapshot test named in this row proved the Snapshot case at commit). The Notification Handler is in a fixture assembly of its own, `ModularMonolith.Tests.Unowned`, since every handler of the Stub's assembly belongs to the Stub. Replaces `SnapshotTests.A_snapshot_declared_without_its_module_in_a_host_of_modules_fails_the_operation_that_would_publish_it`. |
| Every Module the Host adds counts as composed, so a declaration without its Module fails the build even when no Composition Root makes a Kit registration; a Host-level declaration naming a Module the Host never added fails the build too | `CompositionCheckTests.A_declaration_without_its_module_fails_the_build_of_a_host_whose_modules_make_no_kit_registration`; `CompositionCheckTests.A_declaration_for_a_module_the_host_never_composed_fails_the_host_when_built` | Review finding F4. Red once with `ModulesBuilder.Add`'s recording removed, and with the never-composed rule switched off. |
| A Composition Root that names another Module is refused while the Host is composed | `CompositionCheckTests.A_composition_root_that_names_another_module_is_refused_while_the_host_is_composed` | Red once with the refusal removed. |
| A `ConfigureContainer` after the Kit's entry stops the Host at start, naming the call, what was lost and the fix | `CompositionCheckTests.A_container_that_a_later_configure_container_replaced_stops_the_host_at_start_naming_the_call` | The only check left at start: the replaced factory ran neither the validation nor the composition checks. Red once with the runner's sentinel switched off. |
| A cacheable query in a Host without caching fails the Host when it is built, naming the queries and `AddPouryaKitCaching()` | `CompositionCheckTests.A_cacheable_query_in_a_host_without_caching_fails_the_host_when_built_naming_the_call` | Red once with the check switched off. The Proving Sample's Host and both templates call `AddPouryaKitCaching()` and build; the plain-services test compositions that hold the Stub's cacheable queries call it too. |
| A command of the Host's Features in a Host without a Unit of Work fails the Host when it is built; the Kit's own delivery commands do not count, so a Host with Wolverine, no declaration and no Unit of Work builds and starts | `CompositionCheckTests.A_features_command_in_a_host_without_a_unit_of_work_fails_the_host_when_built`; `CompositionCheckTests.A_host_with_wolverine_and_no_declaration_or_unit_of_work_builds_and_starts` | Hosts without Modules; the first red once with the check switched off, the second (review finding F3) with every registered command counted. A Module's own Unit of Work is still checked while the Host is composed (`ModuleWiringTests`). |
| A scanned handler of a command from an assembly no registration scans, as a Contracts assembly's, counts as a command of the Host's Features: in a Host without a Unit of Work it fails the Host when it is built | `CompositionCheckTests.A_scanned_handler_of_a_command_from_another_assembly_in_a_host_without_a_unit_of_work_fails_the_host_when_built` | Second review, finding F7: the check counted only a command whose own type was in a scanned assembly. The handler is `ModularMonolith.Tests.Misnamed`'s `SeparateCommandHandler`, the command `Unowned`'s `UnownedCommand`. Red once with the handler's assembly not counted: the Host built. |

## Wave 2 a misconfigured Host fails clearly, never silently, ticket #62

Spec #33 and the API-misuse review of 2026-10-07 with its design-stage Codex dispositions (API-01, API-02, API-04, API-05):
a wrong composition fails at composition where the builder is in hand, when the Host is built or starts otherwise, or
where its mistake is built, with a message naming the fix, and never runs degraded without a word. The checks run at two
moments with one report shape, by the orchestrator's decision of 2026-10-08: composition checks (`ICompositionCheck`)
when the container is built, as #61's fix round runs them, and startup checks (`IStartupCheck`) at `StartingAsync` for
what only the built application shows; Wolverine's queue durability keeps Wolverine's own moment, `StartedAsync`. The
reference baseline is ASP.NET Core 10's `AuthenticationMiddleware`, which sets `IAuthenticationFeature` on every request
it sees, `WebApplication`'s automatic `UseRouting`, `UseAuthentication` and `UseAuthorization`,
`Microsoft.Extensions.Http`'s handler builder filters, and #61's composition-check entry.

## Wave 2 private-feed publication covers the template package, ticket #54

Ticket #54's criterion "Use the existing central packaging, MinVer, CI validation and private-feed consumer path for new or changed Wave 2 packages", with the owner's decision of 2026-10-07: the publication workflow is fixed on the integration branch, and the real private-feed publication of the Wave 2 set runs on `main` with the merge of `feat/wave-2`, never from another branch. This package made no remote write: no push to the GitHub feed and no workflow run.

| Check | Evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|
| What the consumer step did with the template package before this change | Probe: `dotnet pack PouryaKit.slnx -c Release -o <feed>`, then a one-line `Consumer.csproj` with `<PackageReference Include="PouryaKit.Templates" Version="[0.1.0-preview.0.97]" />`, restored as the step restores (the feed folder named `GitHub` in the step's `NuGet.Config` shape, `--packages` and the HTTP and plugin caches isolated) | A silent success: exit 0 with no warning or error. `project.assets.json` lists `PouryaKit.Templates` as a package with an empty target entry, no compile, runtime or build asset; its 142 files are `content/` and metadata. The first `main` publication would not have failed: it would have proven that the nupkg downloads and nothing about its templates. |
| The changed step, run as written against a local feed | A scratch script outside the repository extracts the step's `run:` block from `.github/workflows/package-publication.yml`, replaces the GitHub feed URL with an empty local folder and runs it with `bash -c` from the checkout, with the step's variables (`PACKAGES_DIR`, `RUNNER_TEMP`, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, a stand-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `NuGetPackageSourceCredentials_GitHub`) | On commit `071625d`: exit 0 in 43 s with the packages and `manifest.json` of a `validate.py` run (commit `1dde46f`, version `0.1.0-preview.0.109`, 21 packages), and exit 0 in 42 s with `dotnet pack` output at `0.1.0-preview.0.97`. The step's own `dotnet nuget push` filled the empty folder with all 21 nupkgs; the library consumer restored the 20 library packages; `PouryaKit.Templates` installed from that folder, which the hive's `packages.json` records as its `NuGetSource`; `pouryakit-modular-monolith` and `pouryakit-monolith` were each generated as `Acme.Shop` and as `acme-shop` and restored (7 and 5 projects), each generated Host's closure holding its Kit packages at the manifest's version only. The step summary named the library consumer, the install and the four generated solutions. |
| The template package must come from the feed | The same run with `PouryaKit.Templates` left out of the manifest, so the push never reaches the feed with it | Exit 103 at `dotnet new install`: `PouryaKit.Templates@0.1.0-preview.0.97 is not found in NuGet feeds` naming the GitHub stand-in alone. |
| The install reads the GitHub source alone | That control with the step's `dotnet nuget disable source nuget.org` line removed | The install also searched `https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json`. `dotnet new install` in SDK 10.0.401 ignores package source mapping: `NuGetApiPackageManager.LoadNuGetSources` (`Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Edge`) takes the enabled sources of the working folder's `NuGet.Config`, adds each `--add-source` not already there, and the first source with the exact version wins. |
| Workflow checks | `python3 -c "import yaml…"` on both publication workflows, `actionlint` with `shellcheck`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/releases/publication -p 'test_*.py'`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/packaging -p 'test_*.py'`, `python3 .agents/scripts/check-ai-setup.py` | All passed; the publication checks still extract and run the artifact-verification step unchanged. *Since 2026-10-10 ([ticket #90](#pre-wave-3-capability-docs-adr-0006-and-repository-hygiene-ticket-90)) the test is `scripts/ci/test_publication.py`, run by `build-and-test`'s discovery of `scripts/ci`.* |

Not proven locally: the credentialed install from GitHub Packages. `NuGetPackageSourceCredentials_GitHub` reaches only a source named `GitHub` in a configuration file (NuGet's `PackageSourceProvider` reads `NuGetPackageSourceCredentials_<name>`), which is why the install runs beside the copied `NuGet.Config`; an `--add-source` URL would carry no credentials. The first `main` publication after the merge of `feat/wave-2` is that proof. *It ran on 2026-10-09 and passed: [Wave 2 hosted publication from main](#wave-2-hosted-publication-from-main).* The generated solutions are restored there, not built or tested: `validate.py`'s template consumers build them, run their smoke tests and publish their Hosts from the produced packages.

### A Module's DbContext and the message store on two databases (a recorded probe)

The rule is `UsePouryaKitWolverine`'s: the store is the database of its connection string, "which every Module's
DbContext must also use" ([messaging.md](../.agents/skills/pourya-kit/references/messaging.md#declaring-handlers-and-running-deliveries)). The
probe `MessageStoreDatabaseTests` (commit `3861dc9`, removed in `e71f92e`) composed a Host without Modules on the
fixture's PostgreSQL 18.6 container, WolverineFx 6.46.0: `UsePouryaKitPostgres<StubDbContext>(connectionName: "app", schema:
"stub")` on one new database, `UsePouryaKitWolverine(connectionName: "messages")` on a second, the Stub's Notification
Handlers, and `Publish` and `Subscribe` of `NoteSharedV1`. One command writes a note whose Domain Event the
`ShareNoteNotificationHandler` publishes `NoteSharedV1` for; another writes a note and sends nothing. It asserts nothing;
it wrote what follows.

| Composition | What happened |
|---|---|
| The Module's database fresh, holding no store tables | The Host was built and started; no composition or startup check refused it. The first command threw `Npgsql.PostgresException` `42P01: relation "wolverine.wolverine_incoming_envelopes" does not exist`, from `EfCoreEnvelopeTransaction.PersistIncomingAsync`, called by `WolverineOutbox.WriteAsync` inside `EfUnitOfWork.RunAsync`: Wolverine writes the envelope on the DbContext's own connection and transaction, in the store's schema, so in the Module's database; it opens no connection to the store. The Unit of Work's transaction rolled back: no note in the Module's database, no row in the store's incoming, outgoing or dead-letter tables, no Notification Handler or Integration Event Handler run, and the dispatcher logged `WriteNoteRaisingCommand threw` at Error. The command that sends nothing committed. The mistake surfaces at the first Operation that writes to the Outbox, atomically, not when the Host is built. |
| The Module's database holding the store's tables, left by a Host that used it as its store | The Outbox write went into that copy and committed with the note. The flush after the commit handed both envelopes to the Host's local queues in memory, so the Notification Handler and the Integration Event Handler each ran once, their Receipts and the publication record in `stub.pouryakit_receipts`. Both envelope rows stayed `Incoming`, owned by node 1, in tables the Host's store never reads; the store's own tables stayed empty; nothing was logged at Warning or above but Wolverine's two handler-discovery notices. A stored retry or a recovery after a crash would read the store, which holds none of them (inferred, not run): the Outbox's durability is gone without a word. For the owner's decision, with a candidate check: compare the store's connection string with each `UsePouryaKitPostgres` connection when the Host is built. |

No permanent test: the rule is a documented deployment rule; that the Outbox write joins the Unit of Work's
transaction is pinned by the commit-timestamp tests (`NotificationTests`, `IntegrationEventTests`), which a write on
another connection would turn red; and a test of the fresh-database row would pin the absence of a check.

`dotnet test --project tests/ModularMonolith.Tests/ModularMonolith.Tests.csproj` on this package's tree, merged with
`feat/wave-2` at `b7f0dce`, printed 504 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. No `validate.py` run: the package changes tests and
this record only.

## Wave 2 the message store and every DbContext share one database, ticket #63

Ticket #63, from the two-database probe above: the message store's connection and every connection a Module's or the
application's DbContext uses (`UsePouryaKitPostgres`) must name one database, and a Host that breaks the rule fails when it is
built instead of writing its Outbox where the store never reads it. The probe's two observations stay as recorded. One
composition check in the shape of #62's connection-string checks, `MessageStoreDatabaseCheck` of
`PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine.EFCore`, registered by `UsePouryaKitWolverine(connectionName)`, compares the string
Wolverine was given with the connection EF Core gives each DbContext, whatever configured it, on its hosts, each with its
port, and its database, as Npgsql reads them; it opens no connection. A string that names neither a database nor a user
leaves the database to the client's user, so it fails the build too. Its limit: host names are not resolved
(`localhost` and `127.0.0.1` differ). The DbContexts' connections reach it through one record,
`DbContextConnection` of `PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore`, moved there from #62's `PostgresConnection` so that both
checks read it; no reference was added ([ADR 0004](adr/0004-commit-through-wolverine-ef-outbox.md)'s #63 amendment).

A recorded limitation, from the #62 re-score: a Host made of `AddPouryaKitWeb` alone, with no Cqrs registration,
registers no check runner. The runner comes with the dispatcher's registration (`AddDispatcher` in
`src/PouryaKit.Cqrs/CqrsServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`), which only `AddPouryaKitCqrs` and
`AddPouryaKitCompositionChecks` make, so such a Host starts with its startup checks unrun, `UnmappedEndpointsCheck`
included. It runs nothing degraded: each Module route group begins the request's Operation
(`src/PouryaKit.Web/Endpoints/WebEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs`), and `BeginOperation` resolves the `Operation` only that
registration adds, so the Host fails at its first request instead.

### Package C: a recurring command's schedule survives a dead-lettered occurrence

| Finding | Fix | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| R2 (medium, Claude): a failed occurrence rolled back the next occurrence it had stored with its effect, so once its stored retries were spent it was dead-lettered and nothing stored a next one; the declaration stopped until a replay or a Host start, against plan I.3's "durable replacement for in-memory Quartz stores" and the Glossary's "every occurrence of a cadence" (#45) | `DelayedCommandDelivery` recognises the attempt whose failure sets the occurrence aside, the one numbered beyond `PouryaKitMessagingOptions.RetryDelays` (Wolverine counts an attempt before the handler runs, then takes the retry policy's slot of that number), and before it rethrows stores the next occurrence after now in an Operation of its own unless one waits, through `RecurringCommandStart`'s query and Operation; a successful occurrence still stores the next one in its own commit | `RecurringCommandTests.An_occurrence_set_aside_as_a_dead_letter_stores_the_next_occurrence_which_runs`; `RecurringCommandTests.An_occurrence_that_succeeds_on_its_last_attempt_leaves_only_the_next_occurrence_its_commit_stored` | Inventory's `ReconcileStock` at a one-second cadence, on a database of its own. The first: `DeliveryProbes.FailAfterReceipt` fails every attempt until the first dead letter appears, and no Host starts again and nothing is replayed; each occurrence set aside, read from its dead letter's `DelayedCommandHeaders.Occurrence` header, had three attempts and left no reconciliation or Receipt, and every reconciliation is of a later occurrence, under the system Actor, with its Receipt. Red once with the dead-letter branch off: no reconciliation within 15 s. The second: `FailAfterReceipt` gains a count and fails the first two deliveries, and the store is read while the occurrence's commit is held: one occurrence waits, committed with the reconciliation. Red once with the attempt recognised one too early (`>=`), and once with every failed attempt storing one: two waited. [ADR 0006](adr/0006-independent-delivery-through-a-routed-queue-per-subscription.md)'s #45 amendment has a dated note citing Wolverine's source. |

### Package D: every Unit of Work's DbContext checked against the store; the negative delivery assertion sees broker envelopes

Findings 2 (high) and 6 (medium). `AddPouryaKitEfCore<TDbContext>(connectionName = null)` records the DbContext's
`DbContextConnection` once, where the Outbox attaches, with the connection name `UsePouryaKitPostgres` passes it and none for a
DbContext the application registered itself; `MessageStoreDatabaseCheck` checks every record and `PostgresConnectionsCheck`
only the named ones. `AssertNothingSentAsync` also fails on an envelope Wolverine handed to a sending agent for a broker
while the Operation ran, read from Wolverine's `wolverine-messages-sent` counter on the Host runtime's own `Meter` (the
store deletes a sent envelope), and on one still stored for a broker afterwards (a latched sender hands nothing out).

| Guarantee | Test | Red once |

## Wave 2 the PouryaKit prefix on two registrations, and /alive in every environment, ticket #64

Spec #33 and the owner's decisions of 2026-10-08 on the two rows the final structural review left open (13 and 14 of its dispositions, the section above), taken before the pull request to `main`, whose merge publishes the packages for the first time: after it a rename breaks every project generated from the templates, and a template Host without a liveness endpoint cannot run behind an orchestrator. Three items: the rename, `/alive` in every environment of the service defaults recipe, and two wording alignments in `PouryaKit.Cqrs`.

The rename: `UsePostgres<TDbContext>` (`PouryaKit.Persistence.Postgres`) is now `UsePouryaKitPostgres<TDbContext>`, and `MapUniqueConstraint<TDbContext>` (`PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore`) is now `MapPouryaKitUniqueConstraint<TDbContext>`, with no alias and no forwarder; signatures and behaviour are unchanged. Every section of this record older than this one was proven under the former names, up to `feat/wave-2` at `74b3150` on 2026-10-08. Their API and test names were replaced in place that day, so that each pointer still resolves: the two tests whose names ended `…_naming_use_postgres` and `…_builds_beside_use_postgres` are `CompositionCheckTests.A_module_that_subscribes_but_registers_no_unit_of_work_fails_the_host_when_built_naming_use_pouryakit_postgres` and `MessageStoreDatabaseTests.A_dbcontext_the_application_registered_on_the_message_stores_database_builds_beside_use_pouryakit_postgres`. [ADR 0004](adr/0004-commit-through-wolverine-ef-outbox.md) and [ADR 0006](adr/0006-independent-delivery-through-a-routed-queue-per-subscription.md) keep their text and take a dated amendment each; the plan's section C takes a dated note on its Persistence.EFCore and Persistence.Postgres rows.

Aspire's guidance (https://aka.ms/aspire/healthchecks, "Non-development environments", read on 2026-10-08): its template maps neither health endpoint outside Development, and a project that enables them protects them with host filtering, authorization or both, and considers a request timeout and an output cache against abuse. The recipe maps `/alive` alone there, anonymous by the owner's decision since an orchestrator's probe carries no token, with no request timeout and no output cache because its one check, `self`, is in-process and constant, and leaves host filtering to the deploying project; a Host that tags a check that leaves the process `live`, or maps `/health` outside Development, takes Aspire's protections with it (`host-recipes.md`, "Liveness and readiness").

Two behaviours stay as they were by the owner's decision of the same day: a command the application owns in a Host of Modules still fails at its first dispatch, naming the fix, not at the build (thread T29), and the bearer scheme's `ClockSkew` takes no cap (T03).

## Wave 2 a repository write outside a Unit of Work is refused, ticket #67

Spec #33. The owner's instructions of 2026-10-08, after ticket #66: find the repository writes made outside a command, refuse the silent loss with a clear exception without breaking a legitimate use, and record in an ADR the decision that made `Operation.IsUnitOfWorkActive` public. With them, the two findings of Codex's second review of pull request #65 that hold (T43, T44).

The repository's two write members, `AddAsync` and `Remove`, checked only `Operation.MayChangeState`, which is true in a scope that runs no command, so the DbContext tracked the change and the scope dropped it. They now also refuse where `Operation.IsUnitOfWorkActive` is false, after the reading check, with `The repository of {Aggregate} was asked to write while no Unit of Work is active, so no commit would save the change and it would be lost. Write from a command's handler, a Domain Event Handler, or a Notification or Integration Event Handler.` No read member and no constructor is guarded, no public member was added, and `IUnitOfWorkConnection.Join()` keeps its own check. Every call of `AddAsync` and `Remove` in `src/`, `samples/`, `tests/`, the templates and the clean consumers was read before the guard was written: each is in a command's handler, a Domain Event Handler, a Notification Handler or an Integration Event Handler, a delayed command's run, or one of the two cases the reading check already refuses.

| Scenario | Proven by | Red once |
|---|---|---|
| In a Host of Modules, `AddAsync` and `Remove` called in a begun scope that sends no command, and in one whose command has already committed, throw the message in full, naming the aggregate and who may write, and `stub.notes` holds what it held: the note to add is absent and the note to remove is still there | `RepositoryTests.A_repository_write_in_a_scope_of_a_host_of_modules_that_runs_no_unit_of_work_throws_and_saves_nothing`, both scopes, against PostgreSQL: the note to remove is found through the repository in the same scope, which needs no Unit of Work | With the check off, in both scopes: the stored rows were as asserted, so nothing was saved, and `AddAsync` had returned (`Assert.IsType() Failure: Value is null`). With the guard left out of `Remove` alone, `Remove` returned the same way and the row stayed. |
| In an application without Modules, the same in a begun scope and in a scope never begun, where no Module's router refuses first | `SingleModuleTests.A_repository_write_in_a_scope_that_runs_no_unit_of_work_throws_and_saves_nothing`, both scopes, on a plain service collection over the Stub's DbContext | With the check off, in both scopes: the stored rows were as asserted and `AddAsync` had returned; with the guard left out of `Remove`, so had `Remove`. |

The rule cannot cover a change made directly to an aggregate loaded through the repository, or a Domain Event raised on one, in a scope that runs no command: no call of the Kit is made there, so nothing can refuse it, and the tracked-state comparison runs only at the end of a query, a check or a reading step. The Kit's own write seams (`IReceipts`, the Outbox buffers, `IUnitOfWork.DbContext`) stay unguarded because the structure test closes them to a Module; a Host's own assembly is not judged by it. Both are recorded in the ADR's amendment.
