## Wave 2 a repository taken outside the dispatcher's pipeline, ticket #68

The follow-up the final audit opened ([its row above](#wave-2-final-audit-before-the-pull-request-to-main)). The owner's decision of 2026-10-09: a text rule over the monolith template's own files, the wording of the gap corrected after a runtime proof, and the ticket closed with its limit named. Tests and docs only: no package, no public member and no runtime behaviour changed.

In an application without Modules the request scope holds the application's own Unit of Work, so an endpoint or a service that takes a repository can load an aggregate and change it outside a command, and no call of the Kit is made there to refuse it. ADR 0003 and the Kit's skill said such a change "is still lost without a word". Run against PostgreSQL, that holds where the scope sends no command; a command the scope sends after the change, if it succeeds, saves it.

| Scenario | Proven by | Red once |
|---|---|---|
| None of the monolith template's own files, its Composition Root, its five endpoints, the Host's `Program.cs` and the smoke test both templates share, takes a repository: no parameter, field or local of `IRepository<,>` or of an interface the Proving Sample derives from it (`IProductRepository` today, read from the sample's files), and none asked of a service provider. The Composition Root's registration of `IProductRepository` takes nothing and is not refused | `TemplateTests.None_of_the_monoliths_own_files_takes_a_repository`: the rule `TemplateRules.RepositoriesTaken` over `content/monolith` and `content/shared`, read as text. Its offending set gets exactly three messages: an endpoint whose lambda takes `IRepository<Product, ProductId>`, a service whose constructor takes `IProductRepository`, and a `Program.cs` that asks a service provider for one under a comment that names `IProductRepository`. Each names the file and the fix: `… takes IProductRepository; send a command through IDispatcher instead: a handler takes the repository, and a change made outside a command is dropped or saved by a command that never made it.` | Six runs, each with one part of the rule off, and the test failed in each: the rule reading no file (no message); the derived names not read from the sample (the service's message missing); comments not left out (a fourth message, for the comment); a declaration not counted (the endpoint's and the service's messages missing); a service provider's answer not counted (the `Program.cs` message missing); and any naming counted, where the shipped `CatalogModule.cs` was refused for its registration. |
| In an application without Modules, an aggregate found through the repository in a begun scope that sends no command, and changed there, is dropped with the scope: nothing throws and its row keeps what it held | `SingleModuleTests.A_change_to_a_loaded_aggregate_in_a_scope_that_sends_no_command_is_dropped_without_a_word`, on a plain service collection over the Stub's DbContext: a folder created by a command, then found and relabelled in a second scope | No red run: the test shows a limit, not a guarantee, so there is no behaviour to switch off. Observed: the scope ended without an exception and `stub.folders` kept `grey`. |
| The same, then a query sent through `IDispatcher` in that scope: the query is not refused and the change is still dropped, because the tracked-state comparison's baseline is the query's start, which already holds the change | `SingleModuleTests.A_change_to_a_loaded_aggregate_is_not_refused_by_a_query_sent_after_it_and_is_still_dropped` | No red run, for the same reason. Observed: the query succeeded and `stub.folders` kept `grey`. A probe in the same composition, not kept, had the query itself relabel the folder after the change made outside it, and it threw `A query changed a Label the Operation saves. Code that only reads must leave the tracked state unchanged.`: the comparison runs there, and its silence in the test is the baseline's. |
| The same, then a command sent through `IDispatcher` in that scope, which writes another row and succeeds: its commit saves the change made outside it, since the Unit of Work saves the whole DbContext | `SingleModuleTests.A_change_to_a_loaded_aggregate_is_saved_by_the_commit_of_a_command_sent_after_it`: `WriteNoteCommand` writes a note, and the folder's label is stored beside it | No red run, for the same reason. Observed: `stub.folders` held `blue` and `stub.notes` the command's note. |
| ADR and docs | The note of 2026-10-09 under "What the rule cannot cover" in [ADR 0003](adr/0003-single-commit-owner.md)'s amendment of 2026-10-08; `persistence.md`, `commands-queries-validation.md` and `templates.md` of the Kit's skill; `docs/architecture/README.md` (the repository's DbContext, the `TemplateTests` row); the audit's row above | |
| Out of scope | | An exception message or a behaviour. The refused writes of #66 and #67 keep their messages, and the summaries under `src/` that repeat their reason, "no commit would save the change", stay as written: that is exact for a scope that sends no command or whose command has returned, and a write made before the scope's command is refused either way, so no test can show what it would do. One `//` comment in `EfRepository.cs` said "no commit would ever save it" without that limit; the review found it (R2) and, on the owner's word of 2026-10-09, it now says the change would be dropped with the scope or saved by a command the scope sent after it. A comment only: no member, message or behaviour changed. The modular template: a Module of a Host of Modules cannot reach the shape. The three tests change a value; none raises a Domain Event. |

What stays open: code an application adds after `dotnet new` is not judged. The rule reads the files the Kit ships, and no package ships structure rules, so a generated solution carries none. As text, the rule also cannot see a repository reached through an alias, through `typeof`, inside another generic type, or through another type the file takes that itself takes one; its summary says so.

## Pre-Wave 3 WolverineFx 6.48.2, ticket #75

Ticket #75 of spec #74 (finding P2), first and alone so that every later ticket of the initiative builds on it: the five `WolverineFx*` pins move from 6.46.0 to 6.48.2. In 6.46.0, one `ReconnectedAsync` exception while Wolverine rebuilt its RabbitMQ agents after a connection recovery left that listener and every one after it without a consumer, while health stayed green; 6.48.0 repairs it (`JasperFx/wolverine` #4864, #4867). [ADR 0004](adr/0004-commit-through-wolverine-ef-outbox.md)'s #75 amendment records the move. No Kit package's code changed.

The release notes, read on 2026-10-09:

- 6.48.0: one listener failing to rebuild after a connection recovery no longer strands the listeners behind it; each is rebuilt on its own, a failure is retried on a bounded schedule, and channel teardown tolerates a channel the client already closed (#4864, #4867). Its other fixes are for clusters (a route resolves its sending agent on every use; global partition slots; agent restrictions confirmed) and `[Deduplicated]` windows.
- 6.48.1: a global partition slot's backlog resumes on its new owner in the order it was sent (#4863).
- 6.48.2: the leader's matching of agents to nodes, and the rest of its first evaluation, are no longer quadratic in the agent count (#4886, #4893); a newly elected leader holds first-time placements for `DurabilitySettings.LeaderTakeoverHoldEvaluations` evaluations, default 1, standing down while no other node holds an assignment (#4899); lifecycle and soak coverage.
- Neither 6.48.1 nor 6.48.2 changes a path the Kit takes, so 6.48.2 was taken, as the ticket names it. 6.48.3, published at 14:42 UTC the same day after the ticket was cut, spreads blue/green warm-ups over every joining node (#4904, #4909) and commits a chain that reads through `IQuerySession` and sends (#4910, a Marten, Polecat and Fisher seam); it was not taken.

| Scenario | Proven by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| The five `WolverineFx*` pins are 6.48.2 and no other pin changes; the templates' `WolverineFx.RuntimeCompilation` pin follows | `Directory.Packages.props`; both templates' `Directory.Packages.props`, which `TemplateTests` keeps equal to the Kit's | On nuget.org each package is `MIT` with a `net10.0` asset. Against 6.46.0 their only dependency change is `JasperFx`, `JasperFx.Events` and `JasperFx.SourceGenerator` 2.80.2 to 2.81.0, `MIT`. Across the checkout's projects restore moved only those three and `WolverineFx.RDBMS` and `WolverineFx.Newtonsoft`, to 6.48.2; it resolved 312 package versions before and after, the same packages by name, Weasel still 9.41.0 |

The started test Hosts run Solo (`UsePouryaKitTestDelivery`); the Balanced ones are single nodes, such as `Inventory.Host` as a process in Production, where `LeaderTakeoverHoldEvaluations` stands down |

It ran in full: the pins reach every package, so `--since` did not skip, and the packed packages, their clean consumers and both generated solutions restored and built on WolverineFx 6.48.2.

**Follow-up, 2026-10-09: WolverineFx 6.48.3.** At the owner's request, 6.48.3, which the list above records as not taken, was reviewed and run, then taken: the seven pins moved from 6.48.2 to 6.48.3 and nothing else. Its notes: a blue/green warm-up spreads over every green node that joins (#4904); three gaps in that machinery, found by a soak on real dispatcher lanes, are closed (#4909); fleet-scale simulated scenarios, test code only (#4905); a chain that only reads through `IQuerySession` but sends gets its commit, in the Marten, Polecat and Fisher frame providers (#4910, #4912). The tag comparison (16 commits, 21 files) also holds #4903, which the notes leave out: `IgnoreEnvelopes` applies inside a tracked test session's `AddStage` stages. The Kit uses no Marten, Polecat, Fisher, event subscription or tracked session. #4904 and #4909 change the leader's agent placement (`AgentCommandDispatcher`, `AssignmentGrid`, `NodeAgentController.EvaluateAssignments`), which every Balanced node runs, but their new branches act only when the leader moves an agent between nodes, which a single node never does. The started test Hosts run Solo; `Inventory.Host` as its own process in Production is a single Balanced node, and `RabbitMqDeliveryTests.A_product_catalog_creates_is_applied_by_inventory_host_running_as_its_own_process_with_the_operation_context` passed on 6.48.3. No test runs several Balanced nodes on one store, on this release or the last. The nuspecs on nuget.org and in the NuGet cache after the restore agree: each package is `MIT` with a `net10.0` asset, and only dependencies among the `WolverineFx` packages move; restore resolved 312 package versions before and after, which differ only in the seven `WolverineFx*` packages, `WolverineFx.RDBMS` and `WolverineFx.Newtonsoft` among them, while `JasperFx` 2.81.0, Weasel 9.41.0 and `RabbitMQ.Client` 7.2.2 stay. No file of `Wolverine.RabbitMQ` and no health check changed between the tags, so `host-recipes.md`'s statement that Wolverine registers no RabbitMQ health check holds on 6.48.3. The listener repair is the one 6.48.2 took: #4867 (merge commit `cbb1c4e`, 2026-10-07) is an ancestor of V6.48.0, V6.48.2 and V6.48.3 and not of V6.46.0, and the decompiled `Wolverine.RabbitMQ.dll` of 6.46.0 and 6.48.2 differ in exactly its two files, `ConnectionMonitor.cs` (each agent rebuilt in its own try/catch, a failed rebuild retried after 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 30 s) and `RabbitMqChannelAgent.cs` (a teardown that tolerates a closed channel). The drop test above proves recovery after a clean drop and delivery after it, not #4867, and no regression test that uses only the broker exists: every refusal a single-node broker can produce on demand closes the channel at channel level, and 6.46.0's unchanged channel-shutdown hook then rebuilds again, while the exceptions that strand a listener (the client's own disposal errors, a quorum queue without a majority) cannot be produced on demand, and upstream's own regression test injects an internal fake agent the Kit cannot build. The defect was reproduced on neither version. A Kit Host has a second broker listener, not durable in Wolverine's sense whatever the broker lists (its endpoint mode is Inline; decompiled `RabbitMqQueue.cs:258`, `RabbitMqTransport.cs:557-560`): by Wolverine's default `DeclareRequestReplySystemQueue = true` (decompiled `RabbitMqTransport.cs:145`), it listens on an auto-delete `wolverine.response.<guid>` queue through the same listening connection (decompiled `RabbitMqListener.cs:88`), so "every one after it" above can apply to a Kit Host. One such queue per Host, with one consumer, was listed by `rabbitmqctl list_queues -p <vhost>` in the broker's container while the drop test ran; the shared connection is read from the code. A known limit, not a Kit defect: after its last retry, about 68 s after the recovery, 6.48.x gives up, and the agent stays without a consumer until the next connection recovery, still with no health signal. On 6.48.3, `dotnet build PouryaKit.slnx` has 0 warnings and 0 errors; `RabbitMqDeliveryTests` passed 21 (the drop test in 6.7 s), `RecurringCommandTests` 9 and `DelayedCommandTests` 13; `dotnet test PouryaKit.slnx` passed 830, 0 failed, 0 skipped, `ModularMonolith.Tests` in 2m29s against about 2m27s at `687acf6`, where the suite also had 830. `python3 scripts/packaging/validate.py --no-fetch --since 687acf6` on the follow-up's source (commit `900a80c`, before this sentence was added) printed `PASS 21 packages, 24 clean consumers (2 generated from templates, smoke tests passed: template-monolith (-n Acme.Shop) 4, template-modular-monolith (-n acme-shop) 5), negative controls and MinVer proof.` at version `0.1.0-preview.0.30`, the version its manifest records for that commit; it ran in full, since the pins reach every package.

## Pre-Wave 3 public API changes, ticket #81

Ticket #81 of spec #74 (findings D16, D7, D18, A2, A4, A5, A6, A10 and V13): the public API changes the final assessment approved. They are the initiative's only intentional breaks, taken before the first public release because the Kit has no external consumer, so no alias or forwarder is kept. No namespace changed, no package or version pin was added, and no consumer's `using` line changes. `src/PouryaKit.Caching/HybridQueryCache.cs` was added to the brief's files for V13 by the session's decision of 2026-10-10.

## Pre-Wave 3 proofs before fixes, ticket #82

Ticket #82 of spec #74 (findings T1, T2, T3 and P7): four open questions about runtime guarantees, each settled by a run before any fix ticket starts, so that a red result cannot change a fix ticket's scope midway. A red result counts as a confirmed problem only when its failing output repeats on a second run; none is fixed here. Environment of every run: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.401, Docker 29.8.1, `postgres:18.6` through Testcontainers, WolverineFx 6.48.3, `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid` 10.10.0, EF Core 10.0.12, Npgsql 10.0.3.

| Question | Proven by | Result | Red once, or the two red runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1, a runtime guarantee: does a tag eviction hold for a cached query whose handler read before the command committed and returns after the eviction? | A PostgreSQL test of `CachingTests`' shape, not kept in the tree: Catalog's `GetProduct` for the Actor ada, held after its Dapper read by a test probe of `IReadConnectionFactory` whose connection's disposal waits for the test, so the handler has read and not returned; `RenameProduct` then commits and evicts `product:{id}`; the hold is released and ada reads again | **Red.** The rename succeeds and the held read answers the old name, as it should; the read after it answers the old name too, from an entry stored after the eviction, which lives until it expires (5 minutes). `HybridCache` stamps an entry when its run starts and, when one of the entry's tags was evicted while the factory ran, stamps it again when the factory completes, so the eviction does not reach it: decompiled `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid` 10.10.0, `DefaultHybridCache.StampedeState<TState, T>.BackgroundFetchAsync`, `if (!Cache.IsValid(CacheItem))` followed by `CacheItem.UnsafeSetCreationTimestamp(...)` with the time the factory returned. The Kit's skill already states this as a limit ([caching.md](../.agents/skills/pourya-kit/references/caching.md#limits)); the README's "evicted once an Operation commits" does not. The orchestrator sizes the fix | Both runs failed at the last read, on 2026-10-09 at 22:49:50 and 22:50:06 UTC: `Assert.Equal() Failure: Strings differ`, `Expected: "Desk lamp"`, `Actual:   "Lamp"`. The test is a correct test of the README's claim, not of what the Kit's skill records, so it stays out of the tree with its probe. *Since ticket #93 (2026-10-10) the test and its probe are in the tree, the test with a joiner added, and pass: a read in flight across the commit stores nothing ([its section](#pre-wave-3-a-cached-read-in-flight-across-a-commit-stores-nothing-ticket-93)).* |
| T2: does a recurring command's cadence survive a release that changes its command's shape while an occurrence waits in the store? | `RecurringCommandTests.An_occurrence_stored_before_its_command_changed_shape_is_set_aside_and_logged_and_its_cadence_waits_for_the_next_host_start` | **The Host reports it; the cadence does not go on.** Inventory's `ReconcileStock`, hourly, on a database of its own: a Host stores the first occurrence and stops; the occurrence's stored body is rewritten through Wolverine's `EnvelopeSerializer` with the message an earlier shape wrote, its occurrence under a member since renamed; a restarted Host finds it waiting and stores none, and it is then made due. Wolverine cannot read it and sets it aside before the Kit's delivery runs (`HandlerPipeline.TryDeserializeEnvelope`, then `MoveToErrorQueue`): a dead letter at `local://inventory.reconcile-stock/` with `System.Text.Json.JsonException`, "JSON deserialization for type 'Inventory.StockItems.Features.ReconcileStock.ReconcileStockCommand' was missing required properties including: 'occurrence'.", and an Error entry of `Wolverine.Runtime.WolverineRuntime`, "Envelope Envelope #… from PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine to local://inventory.reconcile-stock/ was moved to the error queue", with that exception. No Receipt, no reconciliation, and no next occurrence until the next Host start, which stores the first one after now. That is not the guarantee recorded for a dead-lettered occurrence (the Wave 2 final review's package C, finding R2: the cadence goes on), which covers a failure of the occurrence's handler: an occurrence that no longer reads never reaches `DelayedCommandDelivery`. The orchestrator sizes the fix. *Since ticket #94 (2026-10-10) the limitation stands: no store API of WolverineFx 6.48.3 reads the bodies of one queue's waiting occurrences, so a starting Host does not check them, and the recovery is documented ([its section](#pre-wave-3-a-recurring-commands-cadence-after-an-occurrence-that-no-longer-reads-ticket-94)).* | Red once without `RespectRequiredConstructorParameters` in `UsePouryaKitWireJson`: the old body read with a default occurrence and ran, and the test failed waiting, `Not reached within 15 s: exists (select from wolverine.wolverine_dead_letters where received_at = 'local://inventory.reconcile-stock/')` |
| T3: does the Kit still need `UseEntityFrameworkCoreTransactions(TransactionMiddlewareMode.Eager)` in `UsePouryaKitWolverine(connectionName)`? | The whole suite with the line removed: `dotnet test PouryaKit.slnx` at `4bf4b82`, before any other change of the ticket | **No.** 830 passed, 0 failed, the suite's whole count, in 2m27s; `dotnet build PouryaKit.slnx` 0 warnings. The line and its two `using` directives are removed. What it registered, and why the Outbox and the Kit's pre-built handlers use none of it, is [ADR 0004](adr/0004-commit-through-wolverine-ef-outbox.md)'s #82 amendment | A removal: the passing suite without it is the proof |
| P7: is a delayed command or a recurring occurrence due later than `InboxStaleTime` handed out again, and with what effect? | `RecurringCommandTests.A_delayed_command_and_an_occurrence_due_after_the_stale_time_and_handed_out_again_while_they_run_apply_one_effect_each_and_store_one_next_occurrence` | **Handed out again only when a recovery poll comes while an attempt runs; one effect each, and one next occurrence.** On a database of its own, with a 500 ms stale time: the Stub's `WriteKindChangedNoteCommand` declared as the delayed command `stub.stale-note`, due 2 s after its commit, and `ReconcileStock` every 2 s, the held occurrence being one an occurrence's commit stored, so due a cadence later. Each is held after its Receipt until a copy a recovery poll handed out waits on that Receipt (a `Lock` wait in `pg_stat_activity`), then released: one note and one Receipt for the delayed command, one reconciliation and one Receipt for the occurrence, each delivered at least twice, one occurrence waiting next, no dead letter. A delivery waiting in the store is owned by no node, and the release takes only owned rows (`BumpStaleIncomingEnvelopesOperation`, `owner_id != 0 and timestamp <= cutoff`, decompiled `Wolverine.RDBMS` 6.48.3). In three runs with a temporary dump, not kept, each of the 7 occurrences not held, due 1 to 2 s after it was stored, had one attempt, and each held one had two | Red once with the delivery ignoring a Receipt already recorded (`RunDelayedCommandHandler`): `Assert.Equal() Failure: Collections differ`, `Expected: [[1, 1, 1, 1]]`, `Actual:   [[2, 1, 2, 1]]`, two notes and two reconciliations |
| P7's sentence | `PouryaKitMessageStoreOptions.InboxStaleTime`'s summary no longer tells every Host to set it longer than every retry delay plus every attempt's run, which an hourly occurrence never meets under the 5-minute default. It now reads: "longer than every retry delay together plus every attempt's run, queue wait included (`PouryaKitMessagingOptions.RetryDelays`), it keeps a delivery sent at its commit from going stale, but a delayed command or a recurring occurrence due later than it, as an hourly one always is, runs stale from its first attempt and, held by no instance while it waits, is handed out again only when a recovery poll finds an attempt of it still running"; the summary's last sentence adds that the Receipt keeps a recurring command's next occurrence to one | | |
| Docs | The Kit's skill, `messaging.md` ("The stale-time rule", and under "Recurring commands" what T2 showed); [`docs/architecture/README.md`](architecture/README.md) (the message store's registration, no EF Core middleware mode, and the stale time); ADR 0004 (#82 amendment) and ADR 0006 (a dated note on the #44 amendment, whose "No test pins this" the P7 test now does) | | |

Ticket #83 of spec #74 (finding Q1 and its implementer constraint): the four Kit option types registered with a bare `AddOptions<T>()` are validated at start, each with `Validate` and `ValidateOnStart()` chained at its registration, as `AddPouryaKitJwtBearer` validates the same two claims. An intentional behaviour change: a Host given one of the refused values no longer starts, and the `OptionsValidationException` names the option; before #83 it started and failed at the first request, or never visibly. Environment of every run: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.401, Docker 29.8.1, `postgres:18.6` through Testcontainers, WolverineFx 6.48.3.

| Out of scope | | No change from V1's numbers (below). Q9's other two sites, `Subscriptions.ReservedQueues` and the header-value check, belong to other tickets of the spec |

### V1: the measurement

`EnterQuery` and `EnterChecks` each open a reading boundary, and each captures every tracked entry (`src/PouryaKit.Cqrs/Pipeline/Dispatcher.cs`, `src/PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore/UnitOfWork/TrackedState.cs`). Both stay (ADR 0003): this ticket only sizes them. A throwaway console project outside the repository, built in Release against this branch, measured two things:

- **The second capture per nested query.** A command handler attaches N entities of five scalar properties to a DbContext that never opens a connection, then times 100 nested queries whose handler returns at once. The guard is `EfUnitOfWork`'s (`src/PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore/UnitOfWork/EfUnitOfWork.cs`, `TrackedState.Capture(dbContext, includeQueryLoads: true)` compared when the boundary closes); a switch leaves out the checks boundary's capture, which is what removing it would save. 41 alternating rounds of each shape, medians.
- **The DbContext a Dapper-only read constructs.** In the Proving Sample's Host, built and migrated against `postgres:18.6` but not started, Catalog's `ListProducts` through the dispatcher (an empty first Page: its select and count), 1,001 reads; and 15 rounds of 2,000 scopes of Catalog's Operation, timed and counted with `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()` with nothing more, with its `IReadingStateGuard` resolved, and with its two boundaries opened and closed.

```csharp
// The guard: EfUnitOfWork's, or with the checks boundary's capture left out.
public IDisposable OnlyReading(string step) =>
    SkipChecksCapture && step == "An authorizer or a validator"
        ? NoCapture.Instance
        : new ReadingState(TrackedState.Capture(db, includeQueryLoads: true), step);

// The command's handler: N tracked entities, then 100 timed nested queries.
db.Items.AttachRange(Item.Many(command.Entities));
var started = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();
for (var i = 0; i < command.Queries; i++)
{
    await dispatcher.QueryAsync(new NothingQuery(), cancellationToken);
}

return Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime(started).Ticks;

// A Dapper-only read's guard, per scope: step 0 opens the scope only.
using var scope = host.Services.CreateScope();
scope.ServiceProvider.BeginOperation(context, typeof(CatalogModule));
var guard = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IReadingStateGuard>(); // step 1
guard.OnlyReading("A query").Dispose(); // step 2
guard.OnlyReading("An authorizer or a validator").Dispose();
```

| N tracked entities | One boundary, capture and comparison | A nested query with both captures | With the outer capture only | The second capture | Its share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.3 to 0.9 µs | 1.2 to 2.9 µs | 0.9 to 1.9 µs | 0.2 to 1.0 µs | 19 to 35 % |
| 10 | 8.3 to 9.1 µs | 18.5 to 24.7 µs | 8.5 to 13.4 µs | 10.0 to 11.3 µs | 46 to 54 % |
| 100 | 78 to 79 µs | 162 to 171 µs | 81 to 84 µs | 81 to 86 µs | 50 to 51 % |
| 1000 | 1,087 to 1,162 µs | 2,060 to 2,073 µs | 893 to 905 µs | 1,155 to 1,180 µs | 56 to 57 % |

A Dapper-only read: the read took 877 to 1,194 µs (median); its guard added 21.0 to 21.6 µs and 59,300 to 59,450 bytes per read, 1.8 to 2.4 % of the read: resolving it, which constructs Catalog's DbContext and `EfUnitOfWork`, 20.6 to 21.6 µs and 58,140 bytes, and its two captures of the empty change tracker 0.07 to 0.46 µs and about 1,200 bytes.

The ranges are two runs on 2026-10-10: macOS 27.0.1 (Darwin 27.0.0), Apple silicon, 18 cores, .NET 10.0.12 (SDK 10.0.401), Docker 29.8.1. Other agents' test suites ran beside them (a load average of 6 to 8; in the first run three `postgres:18.6`, a `rabbitmq:4.3.6` and a `redis:8.10.1` container of another suite), so the absolute times are indicative; with 10 or more tracked entities the shares agree between the runs. What they say: the second capture costs about 1 µs per tracked entity per nested query, half of the query's own cost once anything is tracked, and a Dapper-only read pays about 21 µs and 58 KB to construct a DbContext it never uses. Neither number changes code here; the orchestrator sizes any change, and none may remove a comparison.

Red alone, the root's test green, with the walk kept to the root |

A non-key property generated on add only is refused unless its mapping names a generator, the one EF's `IValueGeneratorSelector` returns, whose values are not temporary | `SnapshotTests.A_snapshot_of_an_aggregate_whose_value_a_client_side_generator_sets_carries_the_value_committed` | Red with that exception taken out: `System.InvalidOperationException : A Snapshot of Badge is declared, but Badge.Code is generated by the database when it is saved`. ## Pre-Wave 3 the Web and shared JSON fixes, ticket #86

Ticket #86 of spec #74 (findings P8, V9 under the owner's decision D9, V14 and Q9's Web site): three fixes at the HTTP and wire trust boundary and one idiom. V9 and V14 are intentional behaviour changes. No public API changed: the one new type, `KitBadRequestException`, is internal to `PouryaKit.Web`. No package or version pin was added. The XML summary of `UsePouryaKitWolverine` in `src/PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine/WolverineHostApplicationBuilderExtensions.cs`, outside the brief's files, was changed by one sentence on the session's grant of 2026-10-10, because it restates the wire's reading rule.

| Scenario | Proven by | Red once |
|---|---|---|

## Pre-Wave 3 the registration naming rule and private field naming, ticket #88

Ticket #88 of spec #74, items C1 and C2 with decision D17 (option a): the registration naming rule is written down, and private field naming is enforced by the build. No behaviour, public member, registration name, package or version pin changed: the renames touch eleven private fields and their uses, nothing else. Environment of every run: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.401, Docker 29.8.1, `postgres:18.6` through Testcontainers, WolverineFx 6.48.3.

| Scenario | Proven by | Red once |
|---|---|---|
| The registration naming rule: `Use*` mirrors the verb of the framework call it wraps, applies a representation, or configures existing behaviour, so `UsePouryaKitTestDelivery` keeps its name; `Add*` adds a Capability's services; `Map*` maps; the Host builder is the receiver only when the call needs it. The one exception, by D17, is the Module's messaging vocabulary of ADR 0006: `Publish<T>`, `Receive<T>`, `Subscribe<T, THandler>`, `PublishSnapshot` and `ReceiveSnapshot` keep their names in the Composition Root, beside `AddPouryaKitDelayedCommand` and `AddPouryaKitRecurringCommand` | The "Registration names" line of `.claude/rules/kit-code.md`, under "Design" | A judgement call the reviewer carries; no registration was renamed |
| A private field that breaks the naming rule fails the build: PascalCase for `const` and `static readonly` fields, `_camelCase` for every other private field, mutable statics included, whether `private` is written or implied. `.editorconfig`'s `[*.cs]` section gives three symbol groups of `private` fields, one with the `const` modifier, one with `static` and `readonly` and one with none, and `dotnet_diagnostic.IDE1006.severity = warning`, which the build reads; a naming rule's own `severity`, also `warning`, reaches only the IDE. Rules apply by specificity, so the two PascalCase groups win over the bare one | `dotnet build PouryaKit.slnx`: 0 warnings, 0 errors after the renames below | With the rule added and before any rename, the build failed with 4 errors, all IDE1006 on Core's two fields, each also reported by `Offending.Core`, which compiles Core's sources; the 7 projects that do not reference Core built, and the other 34, the four holding the other nine fields among them, were skipped. Built with warnings not as errors (`--no-incremental -p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false`), all 43 projects compiled and reported 13 IDE1006 warnings and nothing else: the eleven fields below, the eleven the findings counted, and Core's two again in `Offending.Core` |
| A mutable static and an implied-`private` field are held to `_camelCase`; a `static readonly` or a `const` field is held to PascalCase | A throwaway class `NamingProbe` in `PouryaKit.Core.Tests`, built with `dotnet build PouryaKit.slnx` and then deleted. Each field was read and written, so no unused-field warning joined the output | The build failed with exactly 5 errors, one per wrong shape: `static int mutableStatic;` (line 5) and `int impliedPrivate;` (line 6) gave `Missing prefix: '_'`; `private static readonly int _staticReadonly = 1;` (7) gave `Prefix '_' is not expected`; `private const int constant = 1;` (8) gave `These words must begin with upper case characters: constant`; `private static int MutableStaticPascal;` (9) gave `Missing prefix: '_'`. The four valid shapes beside them, a `static readonly` and a `const` field in PascalCase and a mutable static and an instance field in `_camelCase`, gave none |
| Nothing else changed behaviour | `dotnet test PouryaKit.slnx`: 885 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (`ModularMonolith.Tests` 2m35s) | |
| The templates | No file under `src/PouryaKit.Templates/content` is an `.editorconfig`, and the generated solutions' shared props set no `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-one-namespace-per-kit-package.md) leaves them out of the namespace check the same way), so there is no template copy of the rule to keep in step. The sample's business code the templates pack builds under the rule here | |
| Docs and AI guidance | The "Registration names" line of `.claude/rules/kit-code.md`; the comment over the rule in `.editorconfig`. The rule file's "Current idioms" line lists the C# 14 and .NET 10 idioms the build enforces and is unchanged; the Kit's skill, `docs/architecture/` and the top-level docs state no field or registration naming convention | |
| Deviation | In the five constructor assignments of `SynchronizationContextScope` and `Pbkdf2PasswordHasher` where the field and its parameter shared a name, `this.previous = previous;` became `_previous = previous;`: the `this.` qualifier only told the field from the parameter, and no other file in the repository writes `this._` | |

## Pre-Wave 3 a cached read in flight across a commit stores nothing, ticket #93

Ticket #93 of spec #74 settles T1 of [#82's section](#pre-wave-3-proofs-before-fixes-ticket-82), under the owner's decision of 2026-10-10: it is a correctness issue, and the fix is the smallest reliable one that keeps performance and the existing cache guarantees. The defect: a cached query whose handler read before a command committed, and returned after that command's tag eviction, stored its pre-commit answer until it expired (5 minutes for the sample's `GetProduct`). `HybridCache` 10.10.0 stamps an entry when its run starts. When one of the entry's tags was evicted while the factory ran, it stamps the entry again once the factory returns (`dotnet/extensions@52cffc2f91 src/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid/Internal/DefaultHybridCache.StampedeStateT.cs`).

The fix lives in `HybridQueryCache` alone. It keeps an in-process record of this Host's handler runs in flight: a `ConcurrentDictionary` used as a set, each entry a private `RunningRead` holding the run's tags and an `Evicted` flag. A run enters the record when its factory starts, before the handler reads, and leaves it in the factory's `finally`. `EvictAsync` first marks every run in flight on one of the evicted tags, and every run when they include `HybridCache`'s wildcard tag `*`, which evicts every entry; then it evicts tag by tag as before. Once the handler has returned, its answer is serialized and the reading boundary closed, the factory checks its mark last. A marked run throws the existing private `NotStored`, which now carries either the failure's errors or the serialized answer. `HybridCache` therefore stores nothing, in memory or in a distributed cache. Every caller that shared the run catches it and reads that answer back, as from an entry, and the next read runs the handler again.

This is shape c1 of the ticket. A cache hit never runs the factory, so it pays nothing. Shape c2 would need the run's record outside the factory, which every hit would pay for. No lock, timer or second cache layer is involved. `IQueryCache`, the key, the tags, `HybridCacheEntryOptions` and its flags, and every package are unchanged. Environment of every run: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.401 (runtime 10.0.12), Docker 29.8.1, `postgres:18.6` and `redis:8.10.1` through Testcontainers, `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid` 10.10.0, WolverineFx 6.48.3.

### What remains

- **The window in the committing Host.** The Kit checks the mark as the factory's last statement. `HybridCache` then checks the entry's tags (`IsValid`) and stores it (`SetL1`) in the same continuation, `BackgroundFetchAsync`, after the factory's `finally` and the await's return, with `ConfigureAwait(false)` and no queueing. Consider an eviction whose mark lands after the Kit's check and whose `RemoveByTagAsync` lands before `IsValid`. The entry is then stamped again and stored, as before the fix, until it expires. If its `RemoveByTagAsync` lands after `IsValid` instead, the entry keeps the run's start stamp, so the next read finds it invalid. Marking before evicting narrows this to the time between the check and `IsValid`, a few synchronous statements: microseconds, where the defect's window was the handler's whole run. No run hit it.
- **Another Host.** Its runs are not in this Host's record, so an eviction committed here does not mark them. As before, that Host may store an answer read before the commit and keep it until it expires, beside the copies the existing limit already covers.
- **A caller that joins after the commit.** It receives the run's answer, read before the commit, for that one call, because `RemoveByTagAsync` leaves runs in flight alone. The run stores nothing.

### The per-read cost

A throwaway console project outside the repository, built in Release against this worktree's `PouryaKit.Caching`, measured the cost. It composes `AddPouryaKitCaching()` with `AddLogging()` and resolves `IQueryCache`. It calls `QueryAsync` with a cacheable query of its own whose handler returns a completed success at once, in two shapes, each 21 rounds of 10,000 reads after a warm-up of 2,000. The first shape is a warmed hit: one entry read again and again. The second is a miss: distinct keys made before the clock starts, each read once, so each runs the factory. Each round is timed with `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()` and weighed with `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()`, as #84's Q8 was. The build of the tip and the build of the change ran alternately, four times each, under the same load.

| Per read | Tip `b644fe9` | With the change |
|---|---|---|
| Hit, median of a run's rounds | 1,170 to 1,188 ns | 1,143 to 1,216 ns |
| Hit, allocated | 1,024 bytes | 1,024 bytes |
| Miss, median of a run's rounds | 3,263 to 3,605 ns | 3,485 to 3,662 ns |
| Miss, allocated | 1,784.1 bytes | 1,872.1 bytes |

The ranges span four runs each, on 2026-10-10 (load average 5 to 6, with other agents' suites and containers running beside them), so the absolute times are indicative. What they say: a hit costs the same before and after, in time and in bytes, because a hit never runs the factory. A miss allocates 88 bytes more, which is the registration itself: the `RunningRead` (32 bytes), the `ConcurrentDictionary` node that holds it (40 bytes), and the two more references in the run's state, which `HybridCache` keeps in its stampede state (16 bytes). Its time is within the miss's noise. A refused run costs the next read one more handler run. What a commit pays is below.

### The per-commit cost

The ticket's item 5 asks for one lookup per evicted tag. The record is a set of runs, not an index by tag, so a commit's `EvictAsync` passes over every run in flight once per evicted tag and asks whether the run's tags contain it (review F2). An index by tag needs a per-tag entry added and removed as runs start and end. Removing a tag's entry when its last run ends races with a run that registers on that tag meanwhile, and closing the race needs a lock or a retry loop, which the brief rules out; the set needs neither. The pass is bounded by the runs in flight on this Host, its concurrent cache misses, never by the tags ever evicted.

The same harness measured `EvictAsync` of one tag with 0, 10, 100 and 1,000 runs in flight on other tags. Each run is a miss whose handler waits on a task the harness completes afterwards. Each shape ran 21 rounds of 10,000 evictions after a warm-up of 1,000, timed and weighed as above, and the record's size, read through reflection, equalled the runs in flight. The build of the tip and the build of the change ran alternately, three times each, on 2026-10-10 (load average about 2).

| Runs in flight on other tags | Tip `b644fe9`, per commit | With the change, per commit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 130 to 133 ns, 112 bytes | 262 to 278 ns, 216 bytes |
| 10 | 131 to 136 ns, 112 bytes | 717 to 749 ns, 216 bytes |
| 100 | 133 to 145 ns, 112 bytes | 1,329 to 1,381 ns, 216 bytes |
| 1,000 | 131 to 138 ns, 112 bytes | 13,970 to 19,332 ns, 216 bytes |

The tip's eviction is `RemoveByTagAsync` alone. The change adds about 11 to 19 ns per run in flight, at 100 and 1,000 runs, for each evicted tag, and 104 bytes per commit of one tag, its two enumerators, whatever the number of runs. The pass's first shape matched each run's tags with `Any(tags.Contains)` and allocated a delegate and an enumerator per run: 1,136 bytes per commit with 10 runs, 9,712 with 100 and 96,112 with 1,000, and about 30 to 42 ns per run at 100 and 1,000 runs. Iterating the evicted tags outside the runs, and asking each run's tags `Contains`, removed that allocation. For scale, the commit before it is a PostgreSQL transaction of milliseconds. The per-read numbers above were measured before this change, which touched only `EvictAsync`, a method no read calls.

`python3 scripts/packaging/validate.py --no-fetch --since b644fe9` on the ticket's commit `18a22b5`, before this paragraph was added, printed `PASS 21 packages, 24 clean consumers (2 generated from templates, smoke tests passed: template-monolith (-n Acme.Shop) 4, template-modular-monolith (-n acme-shop) 5), negative controls and MinVer proof.` at version `0.1.0-preview.0.52`, the version its manifest records for that commit, with the Release runtime suite at 882 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. It ran in full: 4 of the 12 paths changed since `b644fe9` can reach a package, `src/PouryaKit.Caching/HybridQueryCache.cs` among them.

After the dual review, no high finding and five accepted (F1 to F3 medium, F4 and F5 low: the wildcard, the per-commit cost, the probe's disposal, the skill's wildcard sentence and the other-tag test, each fixed above), the same command on the fix round's commit `3f15c69`, before this paragraph was added, printed the same PASS line at version `0.1.0-preview.0.55`, the version its manifest records for that commit, with the Release runtime suite at 885 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. It ran in full: 6 of the 15 paths changed since `b644fe9` can reach a package.

The gate of item 2, a check at start of each waiting occurrence's body, is a no-go on its first attempt, at its first condition, so the ticket closes with item 1: the recovery procedure and the shape rule, documented. No Kit code changed but one XML summary, and no public member, package or version pin changed. The ticket also carries the fix of the T2 test's `53300` failure in the per-project Debug run, which [#95's section](#pre-wave-3-an-empty-retry-schedule-refused-at-start-ticket-95) recorded. ## Pre-Wave 3 one message-store schema per Host, ticket #96

Ticket #96 of spec #74 (Wolverine issue #4923): instances of one Host share one store and one schema, and two different Hosts never share a schema. Documentation only, by the owner's decision of 2026-10-10: no runtime guard, check or test, and no code changed but one XML summary.

## Pre-Wave 3 the OpenAPI options validated at start, ticket #97

Ticket #97 of spec #74, the fifth option type its problem statement counts: `PouryaKitOpenApiOptions` is validated when the Host starts. An intentional behaviour change: a Host whose sunsets hold one of the four refused values no longer starts, and the `OptionsValidationException` names each refused key. Before #97 a key that names no version threw an `InvalidOperationException` only when Asp.Versioning first read its options, as endpoints were built, at the first request or never, and the other three values were accepted without a word: two keys of one version merged into one policy, the last date winning and both links kept; a relative link was written with a leading `/`; an entry with neither value made an empty policy. No public member, package or version pin changed. `AddSunsets` is unchanged, so its throw stays as a backstop a validated Host never reaches; its parse and the validation's, both through `ApiVersionParser.Default`, are the one duplication the ticket accepts. The shape is a private nested `IValidateOptions<PouryaKitOpenApiOptions>`, registered with `TryAddEnumerable` beside `AddOptions<T>().ValidateOnStart()` as `ConfiguredCors` validates `PouryaKitCorsOptions`, in place of the ticket's literal "shape #83 used", a chain of `Validate(predicate, message)`: a chained message is fixed at registration and cannot name the key, and a sunset dictionary holds several entries (the session's decision of 2026-10-10). Environment of every run: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.401, Docker 29.8.1, `postgres:18.6` through Testcontainers, WolverineFx 6.48.3.

| Scenario | Proven by | Red once |
|---|---|---|
| A key that names no API version (`v1`), two keys that parse to one version (`2` and `2.0`), a `Link` that is not an absolute URI (`/api-v3-sunset`, which the binder reads as a relative `Uri`) and a sunset with neither a `Date` nor a `Link` (`4.0` with no value) each stop the Host at `StartAsync` with an `OptionsValidationException` of `PouryaKitOpenApiOptions`, whose failure line names `PouryaKitOpenApiOptions.Sunsets`, the key, the rule and the fix; two refused entries give a line each. The values are bound from configuration beside the sample's valid `1.0` sunset, as the Hosts bind them, and observed at start, by `ValidateOnStart()`: the test's Host maps no versioned endpoint, so nothing else reads them | `MisconfiguredHostTests.A_sunset_naming_no_version_or_a_version_twice_or_a_relative_link_or_nothing_stops_the_host_at_start_naming_its_key`, five cases | With the key check removed, the `v1` case and the two-entry case went red; with the duplicate check removed, the `2` and `2.0` case; with the absolute-URI check removed, the relative-link case and the two-entry case; with the empty-entry check removed, the `4.0` case; with only `ValidateOnStart()` removed, all five, whose Hosts then started. ## Final quality pass: Core, Domain, Cqrs, Validation and Modularity, ticket #99

Ticket #99 of the final quality pass before the push ([#98](https://github.com/PouryaNoufallah96/PouryaKit/issues/98)): the six low findings a quality scout confirmed in Wave 1 and 2 code of these packages, each fixed at its source with a focused test, and one correction of this record. No public API change: a reflection dump of the exported types of Core, Domain, Cqrs, Modularity and Validation and of every public and protected member, 85 types in 551 lines, is identical before and after. No package or version pin changed, and `PouryaKit.Validation`'s code is unchanged. Environment of every run: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.401, Docker 29.8.1, `postgres:18.6` through Testcontainers, Microsoft.Extensions.* 10.0.12, xunit.v3 4.0.1.

| Item | The fix, and proven by | Red once |
|---|---|---|
| 1. A keyed service of a handler's type | `AddHandler` matched any descriptor of the handler's service type. A correction to the ticket, which says `ImplementationType` throws on a keyed descriptor: on Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions 10.0.12 it returns null, as a probe showed, so the old code read the keyed service as a second handler and stopped registration with a false "has 2 handlers". It now skips keyed descriptors, as Modularity's ownership record does. `RegistrationTests.A_keyed_service_of_a_handlers_type_is_no_handler_and_the_scanned_handler_is_registered_beside_it`: the keyed registration stays, and the scanned handler is registered unkeyed beside it | With the keyed filter removed: `InvalidOperationException`, "PouryaKit.Cqrs.Tests.Module.GuardedByCommandCommand has 2 handlers; exactly one is required." |
| 2. The Gateway's usage errors | The missing-context check and the ownership check ran inside the async core, so they surfaced as a faulted task, where a missing command threw at once. They now run in a method that is not async, which then starts the scoped run, a private async method, so every usage error throws before the caller gets a task and a call allocates no closure for the run. `GatewayTests.A_missing_context_or_an_operation_the_module_does_not_own_throws_before_the_gateway_returns_a_task`: each of the three methods with no context throws `ArgumentNullException` naming `context`; Catalog's command, command with a response and query, and a command no Module handles, sent through the Stub Module's Gateway, each throw `InvalidOperationException`; every case is asserted with `Assert.Throws` on the call itself | With the old Gateway processor: "No exception was thrown", 3 of 3 cases without a context; with that half of the test removed, 4 of 4 operations the Module does not own |
| 3. The failure log's level | The dispatcher joined a failed Operation's error codes before the generated method checked the level. It now calls `LogFailed` only when `logger.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Information)`, and the generated method skips its own check (`SkipEnabledCheck`). `FailureLogTests.A_failed_operation_joins_its_error_codes_only_when_its_log_entry_is_written`: a query fails with two codes of 20,000 characters each, and a logger whose entries switch on and off writes nothing; with entries off the synchronous dispatch allocates less than the 80,004 bytes of the joined codes, with them on at least that | With the old dispatcher, entries off: 82,224 bytes |
| 4. The typed-ID factory | `TypedId.From` called the constructor through `ConstructorInvoker.Invoke(object)`, which boxed the value of every ID the EF Core converter and the Dapper handler read. It now calls a lambda compiled once per ID type from `Expression.New`, which passes the constructor's own exceptions through unwrapped, as the invoker did: `TypedIdTests.Empty_values_are_rejected` and `TypedIdTests.An_empty_id_in_json_is_a_json_error` pass unchanged. `TypedIdTests.An_id_created_from_its_value_allocates_no_more_than_its_constructor`: after one warm-up call, 1,000 calls of `From` allocate what 1,000 `new` calls do | With the old factory: expected 32,000 bytes, actual 64,000 |
| 5. `DispatchTests`' predicate | `DispatchTests.A_unit_of_work_that_reports_a_success_other_than_the_commands_result_throws` asserted only that the message names `IUnitOfWork`, which two other dispatcher messages also do; it now asserts the sentence "returned a success that is not the command's own Result" | With the dispatcher throwing its rollback-only message at that point instead, the new assertion failed ("Sub-string not found") where the old one passed |
| 6. `ClockTests`' rendezvous | The two Operations of `ClockTests.A_domain_event_raised_in_an_operation_takes_its_hosts_clock_and_parallel_operations_keep_their_own` wait for each other with no cancellation, so one that fails leaves the other waiting forever. The test now has a 30-second timeout, reads `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` and passes it to both Operations, and the handler waits with `WaitAsync` on the token it receives | With the second Operation replaced by a failed task: the old test was still running after 120 seconds and was killed; the new one failed at 30 seconds with an `AggregateException` holding "The tuesday Operation failed." and xUnit's timeout |
| 7. This record's lookup rule | The rule row on implementing-type lookup, near the top of this file, and the `TypeLookupTests` row of [`docs/architecture/README.md`](architecture/README.md) said every Kit package but Core asks `ImplementingTypes`; both now name the exception, `PouryaKit.Validation`, which finds its validators with FluentValidation's own assembly scanner on purpose (its [provenance record](provenance/PouryaKit.Validation.md)) | |
| For the owner, not changed here | The scout's reading: FluentValidation's assembly scanner silently skips a generic or an abstract validator, where Cqrs's registration refuses a generic handler loudly | |

The measurement of item 4, once before and once after, a throwaway console project outside the repository referencing the five packages, Release, a million calls of `TypedId.From` for a Guid ID per round, five rounds, allocations read with `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread`:

| | Time per million calls | Allocated per call | First call for an ID type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before, `ConstructorInvoker` | 13.9 to 14.6 ms | 64 bytes | 1.1 ms for the first type, 31 µs for the next |
| After, the compiled lambda | 6.2 to 6.8 ms | 32 bytes | 7.9 ms for the first type, 148 µs for the next |
| `new` of the same ID, both runs | 6.0 to 6.6 ms | 32 bytes | |

The compiled lambda is faster and allocates half, the same as the constructor, so it stays. The same project created an ID whose constructor is private through `From`, and an empty value of it surfaced as `ArgumentException`. Its one-time cost is higher: the first ID type loads the expression compiler, and each later type compiles its own lambda.

## Final quality pass: Web, OpenAPI, Security, Observability, Caching and Testing, ticket #101

Ticket #101 of the final quality pass before the push (#98): the seven confirmed problems of the Web, Security, Observability, Caching and Testing quality scout, fixed at the source. One public API change, item 6: `PouryaKitOpenApiOptions.Sunsets` is declared `IDictionary<string, ApiVersionSunset>`, where it was the concrete `Dictionary<,>`, backed by an ordinal `Dictionary` as before. No other public member, exported type name, package or version pin changed. Two registrations now refuse or ignore what they accepted: a second `AddPouryaKitEndpoints` for a declared route prefix or assembly throws, and a second `AddPouryaKitOpenApi` adds only its `configure`. Environment of every run: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.401, Docker 29.8.1, `postgres:18.6` through Testcontainers, Asp.Versioning 10.2.3, OpenTelemetry 1.19.1.

| Scenario | Proven by | Red once |
|---|---|---|
| Item 1. `AddPouryaKitEndpoints` refuses a route prefix already declared, and an assembly whose endpoints are already declared under another prefix, as `AddPouryaKitApiVersions` refuses a prefix twice: either would map the endpoints twice, and each request to one of them would fail as ambiguous. The prefix is checked before any assembly is scanned. The guard reads every Module's declarations, since a Module's builder enumerates the Host's services | `MisconfiguredHostTests.A_route_group_or_an_assembly_whose_endpoints_are_already_declared_is_refused_when_declared_again`, two cases: `/plain` again with another assembly, and the same assembly under `/other` | With the prefix check off, the `/plain` case went red; with the assembly check off, the `/other` case: `Assert.Throws() Failure: No exception was thrown` |
| Item 2. `HostFixture.DisposeAsync` stops the Host, then disposes it in a `finally`, through `IAsyncDisposable` where the Host offers it, as a `WebApplication` does, and else `Dispose`. It disposes the database container in an outer `finally`, whatever the Host's stop or disposal did; a failure still reaches the caller. `InitializeAsync` passes `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` to the container's start and the Host's start | `HostFixtureTests.A_host_that_fails_to_stop_is_still_disposed_asynchronously_and_the_database_container_with_it`: a derived fixture whose Host, a test double with no services, fails to stop. Its real container starts; `DisposeAsync` throws the stop's exception; the double records one `DisposeAsync` and no `Dispose`; and a connection without pooling to the captured connection string then fails with an `NpgsqlException` | With the old body, red: the double recorded no disposal. With `Dispose` in place of `DisposeAsync`, red: it recorded `Dispose`. With the container disposed after the outer `try` instead of in its `finally`, red: the connection opened |
| Item 3. With the rate limit on, `HttpCallerContext.Resolve` builds the request's Operation Context once: the limiter's partition resolves it, keeps it among the request's features, and the endpoint's Operation begins with that same context, one `OperationId`. It is reused only while the request's endpoint and caller are the ones it was resolved from: a limiter placed before routing saw no endpoint, and authorization placed after the limiter may replace the caller. A resolution that throws is not kept, so a trusted peer's unreadable headers still answer 400 from the endpoint | `WebDefaultsTests.With_the_rate_limit_on_the_limiter_and_the_endpoint_share_one_resolution_of_the_callers_context`: an `IClaimsTransformation` hands out the caller as a principal that counts the reads of its Actor claim; one `/stub/context` request as ada reads it once. `WebDefaultsTests`, the whole class, unchanged, including the unreadable-headers case | With reuse off, red: `("ada", 2)` instead of `("ada", 1)` |
| Item 4. The duration histogram's `Meter` comes from the Host container's `IMeterFactory`, through one internal singleton per container that the dispatcher's factory resolves, so each Host owns its instruments and disposes them with itself; the `ActivitySource` stays static. Every Host has an `IMeterFactory`: `HostBuilder.PopulateServiceCollection` calls `AddMetrics` (Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting 10.0.12, decompiled), and `AddMetrics` itself lives in `Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics`, outside Observability's closure, so `AddPouryaKitObservability` does not call it. OpenTelemetry 1.19.1's meter provider selects meters by name only (`MeterProviderSdk`, decompiled), so an exporter still sees every Host of a process | `ObservabilityTests.A_commands_duration_is_measured_on_a_meter_of_the_hosts_own_meter_factory`: each duration a `WriteNoteCommand` records comes from a meter whose `Scope` is the fixture Host's `IMeterFactory`. The other `ObservabilityTests`, which listen by meter name, and `HostRecipeTests`, which export through OpenTelemetry, pass unchanged | With a static `new Meter(...)` in its place, red: `Assert.Same() Failure`, the scope was null |
| Item 5. `StoredDeliveries.DeleteAllAsync` runs its three `DELETE` statements with `ExecuteNonQueryAsync`, not through a reader | Every `HostTest` resets through it before each test: `ModularMonolith.Tests`, the whole suite | |
| Item 6. `Sunsets` is an `IDictionary` with ordinal keys. Asp.Versioning ignores the case of a version's status (`ApiVersion` hashes `Status` with `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`; Asp.Versioning.Abstractions 10.2.1, decompiled), so `1.0-Beta` and `1.0-beta` name one version: the dictionary keeps both keys, and #97's validation refuses them by name, where a case-insensitive one would keep the last without a word. The binder still binds the interface, the sample's sunset included | `MisconfiguredHostTests.Two_sunset_keys_that_differ_only_in_case_stop_the_host_at_start_naming_both`. The binding: `MisconfiguredHostTests.The_samples_sunset_or_none_lets_the_host_start` and the sunset theory of #97, unchanged | With `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`, red: the Host started |
| Item 7. Verified: Asp.Versioning.OpenApi 10.2.3's `AddOpenApi(configure)` calls `services.Configure<VersionedOpenApiOptions>(configure)` on every call (decompiled), so a second `AddPouryaKitOpenApi` ran each operation transformer twice, and an operation listed its `Idempotency-Key` parameter twice; the sunset `Link` header stayed single. Fixed with the siblings' idiom: a second call adds only its `configure` and returns, found by the sunset validation it registered | `OpenApiTests.A_second_registration_of_the_api_versions_and_documents_adds_nothing`: the sample's Host with one more `AddPouryaKitOpenApi()` lists the header once on each operation that requires it | Without the guard, red: "Sequence contains more than one element" on the duplicated parameter. With the `Link` header asserted first, the header passed, so the test does not assert it |

## Number sequences, ticket #122

Ticket #122 of spec #115: a gap-free number per scope key inside the Unit of Work, as a registration in `PouryaKit.Persistence.Postgres`. A Module calls `AddPouryaKitNumberSequences()` on its builder and creates `pouryakit_number_sequences` with `CreateNumberSequenceTable(schema)`; a handler asks `INumberSequences.NextAsync(scopeKey)` for a `Result<long>`. The allocation joins the Unit of Work's transaction through `IUnitOfWorkConnection.Join()` and sends one Npgsql batch: an insert of the scope row that does nothing on conflict, then an update that adds one and returns the value. The Proving Sample's Inventory numbers its stock counts per year (`StartStockCount`, migration `StockCounts`). Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, Npgsql 10.0.3, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium headless.

| Item | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Two concurrent Operations on one scope key get consecutive numbers, the second waiting | `NumberSequenceTests.Two_operations_on_one_scope_key_get_consecutive_numbers_and_the_second_waits_for_the_first_to_commit`: the first stock count, begun as an Inventory Operation, takes number 1 and is held before its commit; the second, sent through Inventory's Gateway, is seen waiting on a lock on the sequence table in `pg_stat_activity` and has not returned; once the first commits it receives 2 | Red once with the allocation on a connection of its own outside the transaction: the second never waited (`The second stock count did not wait on the first's number sequence row.` after 15 s), though the numbers were still consecutive |
| A rolled-back Operation leaves no gap | `NumberSequenceTests.A_rolled_back_operation_gives_its_number_back_to_the_next_operation`: an Operation that starts a stock count, then fails with an Error, is rolled back; the next stock count receives the number it released, 1, and only that row is stored | Red once with the same own-connection allocation: `Assert.Equal() Failure: Values differ`, the next number was 2 |

## Permission check covers handler-discovered operations, ticket #144

Ticket #144 of spec #115, the permission twin of #116's PR #143 fix. `AddPouryaKitPermissions` registered `PermissionAuthorizer<T>` only for the attributed commands and queries the scanned assemblies declare, while `AddPouryaKitCqrs` also dispatches one a scanned handler handles that another assembly declares, such as a Module's Contracts. ## Tenancy at save and delivery, ticket #117

Ticket #117 of spec #115: Multi-tenancy at the save and delivery seams, as registrations in existing packages. The EF Unit of Work's prepare step refuses with `TenantErrors.Mismatch` (`Tenant.Mismatch`, forbidden) a save of an `ITenantScoped` entity that is not the Operation's tenant's; the delivery step refuses a delivery with no tenant into a tenant-scoped Module before its Receipt; `RecurringCommandTenancyCheck` and `SnapshotKeyTenancyCheck` refuse a recurring command, and a Snapshot of an aggregate whose key two tenants could share, in such a Module; the Receipt and Snapshot version keys stay as built (T1, ADR 0006's #117 amendment). Inventory keys its copies of Catalog's products by tenant and product. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, EF Core 10.0.12, Npgsql EF Core 10.0.3, WolverineFx 6.48.3. ## Dapper tenant rule, ticket #118

Ticket #118 of spec #115: the Dapper part of Multi-tenancy, a structure rule with no runtime seam. `ModuleRules.ReadsBeyondTheTenant` reads every string literal of a Module the Host records as tenant-scoped (`HostComposition.IsTenantScoped`, from the Host `Sample` builds and never starts) and holds each one that reads a table an `ITenantScoped` entity maps to one shape: one `SELECT` with no set operator, no subquery and no top-level `OR` in its `WHERE`, whose `WHERE` has a top-level conjunct `<alias>.tenant = @Tenant` for each such table it reads, or `tenant = @Tenant` when its `FROM` reads that one table. Every other shape is rejected. After the second review it reads the literal's tokens (`Sql.Tokens`) against one allow-list grammar. It reuses `Il` and `Sql` and adds no package. Catalog's `GetProduct` and `ListProducts` keep to the shape as written in #116 and are unchanged. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2. Each red run below changed one or two sources through a scratchpad script that ran the class and restored the files.

| Item | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The rule rejects a top-level `OR`, a `UNION` and an unfiltered join | `Offending.CrossTenantReadingQueryHandler` reads Catalog's tables three times, each naming `tenant = @Tenant`: inside a top-level `OR`, in one branch of a `UNION`, and for `catalog.products` of a join that leaves `catalog.categories c` unfiltered. Each is one violation naming its fault: `has an OR at the top level of its WHERE`, `has the set operator union`, `does not hold catalog.categories c to @Tenant with a top-level conjunct of its WHERE` | `DapperTenantTests.A_top_level_or_a_union_and_an_unfiltered_join_are_rejected_though_each_names_the_tenant`. Red with each weaker predicate: `tenant = @Tenant` anywhere in the text accepted (all three passed, and 13 shape cases); `OR` split as `AND` (the `OR` read passed); only the text before a set operator judged (the `UNION` read passed); one tenant-scoped table of a read held to the tenant enough (the join passed) |

## Web conventions for other transports, ticket #119

Ticket #119 of spec #115, the Web prefactor gRPC (#134) builds on: two public members, nothing else changes. `BeginOperationPerRequest()` on a `RouteGroupBuilder` is the begin-the-Operation convention `MapPouryaKitModuleEndpoints` applies to each Module's group; `OperationContextHttpHeaders`, Web's one codec, is public with one public member, `Pairs(context)`, which the outgoing handler writes. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium headless.

## Email, ticket #124

Ticket #124 of spec #115: the email contract `PouryaKit.Email` (`IEmailSender.SendAsync(EmailMessage, CancellationToken)` returning a `Result`, `EmailErrors.InvalidAddress`), on Domain alone, and the MailKit sender `PouryaKit.Email.MailKit` (`AddPouryaKitMailKit()`, `PouryaKitMailKitOptions`), a singleton built in its registration's factory from options the Host binds from `PouryaKit:Email` and the Kit validates at start, sending on a connection per send from one registration, the choice spec #115 left to the ticket. `ModularMonolith.Host` composes it; the Stub's Notification Handlers (`tests/ModularMonolith.Tests/Stub/StubEmail.cs`) send. `EmailTests` runs the application on a database of its own with its mail sent to a Papercut container (`changemakerstudiosus/papercut-smtp:7.8.0` through `Testcontainers.Papercut` 4.15.0) and reads what arrived from Papercut's HTTP API. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, MailKit 4.18.1.

|---|---|---|

## Localization, ticket #125

## File storage, ticket #127

Ticket #127 of spec #115: the file storage contract, `PouryaKit.Storage`, and its S3 provider, `PouryaKit.Storage.S3`. `IFileStorage` uploads, downloads and deletes a file under a key the caller chooses and signs a time-limited link, each call with a `CancellationToken` and returning a `Result`. `AddPouryaKitS3Storage()` registers it from `PouryaKitS3StorageOptions`, which the Host binds from configuration and which are validated when it starts. The proof is its own test project, `tests/PouryaKit.Storage.Tests`, with MinIO in Testcontainers: no criterion needs the Proving Sample to compose storage, and a provider test needs no PostgreSQL. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, `AWSSDK.S3` 4.0.104.4, `minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-04-22T22-12-26Z` (replaced by `rustfs/rustfs:1.0.2` on 2026-10-17, #148, after MinIO withdrew its images), Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium headless.

## Outgoing HTTP cancellation test, ticket #149

Ticket #149 of spec #115: `OutgoingHttpTests.Cancelling_the_call_stops_further_attempts` cancelled on a 300 ms timer and waited 3.5 s before counting attempts, and failed in CI on untouched commits when the first attempt had not reached WireMock.Net before the timer fired. Test-only; no production code changed. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2.

| Criterion | Test or change | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The test fails when the cancellation does not stop further attempts, and passes without a timing margin | A test handler, innermost below the resilience handler, cancels the call once the first attempt's 503 has come back, before the pipeline decides on a retry. The attempts run inside the awaited call, so the journal is counted as soon as the call has ended: no timer and no wait | Red once with the call sent without the cancelled token: `Assert.ThrowsAny() Failure: No exception was thrown`, the pipeline retried to its limit and returned the 503. Red once more with the call also out of `ThrowsAny` (its cancellation caught), so the count is reached: `Assert.Single() Failure: The collection contained 4 items`. Both edits reverted. Ten runs of `OutgoingHttpTests` (16 tests each): 10 passed, 0 failed |
| No production code changes; the whole suite stays green | No `src/**` change: `tests/ModularMonolith.Tests/OutgoingHttpTests.cs`, this document and two agent-memory notes (`.claude/agent-memory/kit-implementer/`) changed; the skill's web reference states the behaviour, not the test's mechanism | `ModularMonolith.Tests`: 685 passed |

## Provider guarantees, ticket #147

Ticket #147 of spec #115, raised by three Codex threads on PR #143 after #124 and #127 closed: the one-provider guarantee of `PouryaKit.Storage.S3` and `PouryaKit.Email.MailKit` holds whatever the registration order, and an S3 presigned link refuses a lifetime S3 cannot sign. Each provider registers an internal composition check, `OneFileStorageCheck` and `OneEmailSenderCheck`, with `TryAddEnumerable`; it fails the Host's build when two or more unkeyed `IFileStorage` (or `IEmailSender`) registrations are in its final composition, naming each registration's type, or the factory that builds it. The first round put the check in an options validation at start, because the contract and provider packages referenced no Cqrs; the dual review's F1 held that a built Host runs Operations through its Gateways before it starts (#61 F1), and the orchestrator's scope decision gave both providers a reference to `PouryaKit.Cqrs`, the contracts staying on Domain alone. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, `AWSSDK.S3` 4.0.104.4, MailKit 4.18.1, `rustfs/rustfs:1.0.2`, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium headless.

## PR #143 review round after batch 2, ticket #150

Ticket #150 of spec #115: three Codex findings on PR #143 after the batch 2 closes. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, MailKit 4.18.1, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium headless.

| Criterion | Test or change | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A disconnect failure after acceptance leaves the send successful | No code change (session's disposition): MailKit 4.18.1's `SmtpClient.DisconnectAsync(quit: true)` already wraps the QUIT in `catch` blocks for `OperationCanceledException`, `SmtpProtocolException`, `SmtpCommandException` and `IOException`, then closes the connection, and `SmtpStream.FlushAsync` turns a cancelled token into an `OperationCanceledException` that lands there. A server that drops, resets, refuses or times out on QUIT, and a cancellation after `SmtpClient.SendAsync` has returned, leave `MailKitEmailSender.SendAsync` successful today; a cancellation before that return (MailKit reads the DATA response with the caller's token and rethrows), the window between the server's 250 and MailKit reading it included, fails the send and is the sent-twice limit. A guard of the Kit's own could not be shown red, so none was added. Disposition (orchestrator, review F2): criterion 1's "red once with the guard off" is not met by design; the claim rests on MailKit 4.18.1's source, not on a runtime test of the Kit's, and the skill says so. Any other exception after acceptance is the stated limit, a mail sent twice by the retry, which `EmailTests.A_mail_whose_delivery_fails_after_sending_it_is_sent_again_by_the_retry` still proves. The skill's [email.md](../.agents/skills/pourya-kit/references/email.md) states it in the sender's paragraph | `ilspycmd` of `MailKit.dll` 4.18.1 (`lib/net10.0`): `SmtpClient.DisconnectAsync` and `SmtpStream.FlushAsync` |

## Ownership at save for attached entities, ticket #152

Ticket #152 of spec #115, a Codex thread on PR #143: an entity attached or updated with a key it was given and the caller's tenant was judged by that tenant, so its UPDATE or DELETE could reach another tenant's row. The owner chose tenant-aware writes (2026-10-17): `PouryaKitModelConvention` makes every tenant-scoped root entity's `Tenant` a concurrency token beside `Version`, so every UPDATE and DELETE of such a row carries the tenant the entity was loaded or attached with. The review's F1 showed a part, which has no tenant column, still reached another tenant's row by its key alone; the owner's rule for the fix round: cross-tenant updates and deletes are blocked, attached entities included. The prepare step now refuses with `TenantErrors.NotLoaded` (`Tenant.NotLoaded`, forbidden) a changed or removed tenant-scoped entity, a part of one, or an aggregate a change is attributed to, that no query of the DbContext loaded (`PouryaKitDbContext` records them from EF Core's `ChangeTracker.Tracked` event when `FromQuery` is true, and forgets one tracked again without a query, review F3); an added entity is new, not attached. The `Tenant.Mismatch` check runs first, unchanged, and the token stays, the guard for a write that reaches the database. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, EF Core 10.0.12, Npgsql EF Core 10.0.3.

|---|---|---|

Fix round, red with the refusal off: all three cases failed on north's own row (counted, renamed, deleted) while south's stayed `south, Lamps, 0, 1`, the token stopping it |

## Tenant filter for aggregate parts, ticket #153

Ticket #153 of spec #115, a Codex thread on PR #143 after #152 closed: `PouryaKitModelConvention` gave `PouryaKitDbContext.TenantFilter` only to `ITenantScoped` roots, so a Feature querying a navigation-held part through its own set (`Set<Sheet>()`) during one tenant's Operation read every tenant's parts. The convention now gives each such part, at any level of a tenant-scoped aggregate (the holder walk #152 added), the same named filter: for each key to a holder, an `Any` over the holder's `EntityQueryRootExpression` matching that key, so the part passes only where its holder is read through the holder's own filters, the root's tenant filter or, for a part of a part, its holder's part filter. The tenant is still read only by the root's filter, each time a query runs. `IgnoreQueryFilters([TenantFilter])` sets a part's filter aside as it sets a root's. No migration: a filter changes no column. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, EF Core 10.0.12, Npgsql EF Core 10.0.3.

| #152's forged-holder and reattach proofs still run | The Stub's `ReattachSheetCommand` and `ForgeSheetHolderCommand` read south's sheet with the tenant filter set aside, their comments saying so in place of "which no tenant filter reads" | `TenantOwnershipTests`: 24 passed, #152's 23 included |

## PR #143 review round after #153, ticket #154

Ticket #154 of spec #115, three Codex threads on PR #143 after #153 closed. The Dapper tenant rule (#118) found tenant-scoped tables from `ITenantScoped` entities only, so a literal reading the table of a navigation-held part (#153's model), which has no tenant column, was not judged. `ModuleRules.TenantTablesOf` now also yields each such part's table, a part of a part too, with its keys to its holders, found by `PouryaKitModelConvention`'s walk; the grammar holds a part's item only when an `ON` joins it, `part.column = holder.column` for every column of one key, to a held item of its holder, up to a root held by `tenant = @Tenant` (the part's own `ON`, or the holder's when that is no `LEFT JOIN`). The presigned-link contract names the credentials' lifetime, and `HeaderRequestCulture` tries 16 Accept-Language values, not every one.

## Dapper tenant binding in the lease, ticket #155

Ticket #155 of spec #115, the owner's decision of 2026-10-17 on PR #143's review thread `PRRT_kwDOU7M5js6thcB6`: #118's structure rule proved the shape of a read's tenant predicate but not the value a handler bound as `@Tenant`, so the spec's "Dapper: no runtime seam" is amended. `IReadConnectionFactory.OpenAsync` sets the PostgreSQL session setting `pouryakit.tenant` on each lease, after it opens, with a parameterised `select set_config('pouryakit.tenant', @tenant, false)`, to the tenant of the scope's Operation read when the lease opens, or to the empty string, which matches no row, where the Operation has none or none began. The factory is now one per scope (the scope's `Operation`) over the Host's one Npgsql data source, a singleton keyed by the factory's type that the Host still disposes; `AddPouryaKitDapper` keeps its signature and `IReadConnectionFactory` its member. A tenant-scoped read compares `tenant = current_setting('pouryakit.tenant')`; `ModuleRules.TenantReadFault` admits exactly that conjunct (one word `current_setting`, parentheses, one string literal `pouryakit.tenant`) and rejects `@Tenant` or any other right-hand side with a fault naming the required conjunct, the grammar otherwise unchanged. Catalog's `GetProduct` and `ListProducts` compare it and bind no tenant. No wrapper, no new package, no row-level security.

## BeginOperationPerRequest once per endpoint, ticket #156

Ticket #156 of spec #115, raised by Codex on PR #143 (thread `PRRT_kwDOU7M5js6tivEr`): `BeginOperationPerRequest()` added a `Finally` wrapper on every call, so an endpoint under a root group and a nested group that both call it began its Operation twice and answered 500 ("already begun"). The wrapper now adds a private marker to the endpoint's metadata and returns where one is already there, so the convention applies once per endpoint. The public signature is unchanged.
