## Per-Module stores and the store-neutral Outbox, ticket #121

Ticket #121 of spec #115, the prefactor #131 and #132 wait on, with the three invariants ADR 0011 assigns it. Each persistence registration on a Module's builder keys that Module's `IIdempotencyStore`, and `PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine.EFCore` keys `EfReceipts` for every Module that keys no Receipts of its own (`KeyedService.AnyKey`); Cqrs's `IModuleServices.RouteByModule` replaces each unkeyed registration with a resolver by the Operation's Module whenever a Module is composed, and a Host without Modules keeps its unkeyed stores. The route filter, the Operation Context headers and tracestate, an Integration Event's identity header and publication record, and the Snapshot and delayed-command headers moved from the EF Outbox to `OutboxWriter` in `PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine`, with the two scope buffers and the store-neutral half of the message store's registration, `UsePouryaKitMessageStore` with `PouryaKitMessageStoreOptions`; `PouryaKitIdempotencyOptions` and its validation moved to Cqrs (`AddPouryaKitIdempotencyOptions`). No package was added. By the session's decision of 2026-10-18, section C is unchanged: `PersistMessagesWithPostgresql` is the delegate a store package passes, and the store database check stays in the EF package (ADR 0011's dated note).

| Criterion | Test or change | Evidence |

Red once with no resolver, and once with the EF Receipts not routed: all three orders failed |

## Reverse proxy, ticket #126

Ticket #126 of spec #115: `PouryaKit.ReverseProxy`, for a Host of its own process on YARP. `AddPouryaKitReverseProxy()` loads routes and clusters from the `ReverseProxy` section, adds service discovery's destination resolver and the internal `LivenessProbe` configuration filter, which turns on each cluster's active health check at `/alive` unless the cluster's configuration says otherwise; YARP's defaults stay, so nothing is stripped and its default propagator sends the proxy's own span. The Proving Sample's `ModularMonolith.ReverseProxy` composes it with the service defaults, and each template generates its own copy, `src/<name>.ReverseProxy`. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's headless Chromium 1243.

The cluster's one destination, `http://modular-monolith`, resolves through `Services:modular-monolith:http` into the Host and an unbound port; after the probes the Host is `Healthy`, the unbound port `Unhealthy` and out of `AvailableDestinations`, and four requests through the proxy answer 200 | Red once with `AddServiceDiscoveryDestinationResolver()` removed: all three tests failed, the destination never resolving. ## Reporting renderer, ticket #129

Ticket #129 of spec #115, user stories 62 and 76: `PouryaKit.Reporting`, the optional renderer, on the libraries of the spec's E1, `PDFsharp-MigraDoc` 6.2.4, `DocumentFormat.OpenXml` 3.5.1 and `CsvHelper` 33.1.0. `IReportRenderer.Render(ReportLayout, ReportFormat)` renders a Module's layout (a title, headings and paragraphs, one table of text cells, a logo and an accent colour, a page header and footer) to a `RenderedReport` with the file's bytes, content type and extension, or refuses it with `ReportErrors.TableShape` or `ReportErrors.LogoFormat`. The package references Domain alone and stores nothing; the report Module is #140. No container is needed, so the proof is its own test project, `tests/PouryaKit.Reporting.Tests`. ## Aspire resources, ticket #130

Ticket #130 of spec #115: `PouryaKit.Aspire`, AppHost-only, on `Aspire.Hosting.PostgreSQL`, `.Redis` and `.RabbitMQ` 13.6.1, and the Proving Sample's `ModularMonolith.AppHost`. `AddPouryaKitPostgres`, `AddPouryaKitRedis` and `AddPouryaKitRabbitMq` add each container on the tag the Kit's Testcontainers fixtures run, with a named data volume. An AppHost cannot see a Host's registrations, so its author calls Redis and RabbitMQ for the Hosts whose composition uses them and gives each Host its resources under the connection names it reads. The proof is its own test project, `tests/PouryaKit.Aspire.Tests`, on `Aspire.Hosting.Testing`: it uses none of `ModularMonolith.Tests`' fixtures, since the AppHost starts the Hosts as processes. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium headless.

## Stream write model, ticket #131

Ticket #131 of spec #115, user stories 17 to 24: the Stream write model as Spike #120 proved it and ADR 0011 records, in two packages. `PouryaKit.Persistence.Marten` (Cqrs, Persistence; `Marten` 9.46.0, and `Npgsql` at the Kit's line) holds `StreamAggregate`, `IStreams`, the Marten Unit of Work, its idempotency store and cleanup, and the Host's one Marten store (`AddPouryaKitMarten`); a Module calls `AddPouryaKitStreams(schema)`. `PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine.Marten` (Messaging.Wolverine, Persistence.Marten; `WolverineFx.Marten` 6.48.3) integrates the store with the Kit's message store, writes the Outbox through `OutboxWriter` into a `MartenOutbox` on the Unit of Work's session, and keys each Stream Module's `MartenReceipts`; a Host calls `UsePouryaKitMarten(connectionName)`, after `UsePouryaKitWolverine(connectionName)` when it also has EF Core Modules. The Receipt and idempotency statements are now one copy each, `ReceiptStatements` in Messaging.Wolverine and `IdempotencyStatements` in Persistence, which the EF packages run too; `UnitOfWorkErrors` moved from Persistence.EFCore to Persistence; the EF package's `MessageStoreDatabaseCheck` reads the Marten store's `OutboxConnection`. The proof shares `ModularMonolith.Tests`: `StreamTests` over the test Stream Module `tests/ModularMonolith.Tests/Streams` (Accounts), in a Host of Accounts alone (`StreamHost/StreamHosts.cs`, also run as an OS process) and in the Proving Sample's Host with Accounts beside its EF Core Modules, each test on a database of its own in `StreamFixture`'s PostgreSQL 18.6. The sample's `Ledger` is #132's.

## Ledger Stream Module, ticket #132

Ticket #132 of spec #115, user story 25: the Proving Sample's first Stream Module, `Ledger`, on the Marten packages of #131, beside the EF Core Modules Catalog, Inventory and Billing in `ModularMonolith.Host`, which registers its Marten store with `UsePouryaKitMarten(connectionName: "app")` after `UsePouryaKitWolverine` (ADR 0011's mixed Host). Ledger is tenant-scoped (`AddPouryaKitTenancy`), since the store is conjoined, and keeps its Receipts and keys in the `ledger` schema. `OpenAccount` starts an account's Stream, `PostEntry` appends an entry at the version it read, and `GetAccount` is the projection, the account's fold through `IStreams.LoadAsync`; its endpoints are `POST /ledger/accounts`, `POST /ledger/accounts/{accountId}/entries` and `GET /ledger/accounts/{accountId}`. `ActivateAccountNotificationHandler` appends the account's activation and publishes `AccountOpenedV1` (`Ledger.Contracts`, `ledger.account-opened.v1`) in one commit with its Receipt; Billing's `OpenWelcomeQuoteIntegrationEventHandler` (`billing.account-opened`) opens a welcome quote, under an id derived from the delivered tenant and the account (`QuoteIdOf`), and schedules its expiry. The modular template gains Ledger; the monolith does not, since a Host without Modularity holds one Unit of Work.

## Realtime, ticket #133

Ticket #133 of spec #115: the optional `PouryaKit.Realtime`, referencing `PouryaKit.Web`, `PouryaKit.Persistence.EFCore` and `Npgsql`, as the spec's Realtime decision places it, with the mechanism of its decision R1, recorded in [ADR 0012](adr/0012-realtime-through-postgresql-notifications.md): `IRealtimePublisher` writes `pg_notify` on the delivery's own transaction, one listener per instance hears every committed push, and `MapPouryaKitRealtime` serves `TypedResults.ServerSentEvents` from the instance's clients keyed by tenant and Channel. The Proving Sample's `AnnounceNewProductNotificationHandler` pushes `NewProduct` on `catalog.new-products`, which Catalog's `NewProductsRealtime` serves. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker, `postgres:18.6` in Testcontainers 4.15.0, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium.

| Criterion | Test or change | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A Notification committed on instance A reaches a client connected to instance B, two instances of one Host on one store under Balanced durability | `RealtimeTests.A_product_committed_on_one_instance_reaches_a_client_connected_to_another`: two sample Hosts started on the fixture's database, each with `PouryaKitMessageStoreOptions.Durability` set back to Balanced after the test delivery's Solo (the review's F2); a client of the second listens on `catalog.new-products`, and a product created through the first, whose local queue holds the Notification, arrives as `{"productId":…,"name":"Lamp"}` | Red once with the push handed to the publishing instance's clients instead of `pg_notify`: no event within 20 s |
| A delivery that rolls back emits nothing | `RealtimeTests.A_push_whose_delivery_rolls_back_reaches_no_client`: a Stub Notification Handler pushes "1" and fails its first delivery, then pushes "2" and commits; the client's first event is "2" | Red once with `pg_notify` run on a connection of its own outside the delivery's transaction: the first event was "1" |
| A push is callable only from a Notification Handler's delivery | The delivery step records the Domain Event a Notification Handler's delivery delivers in that delivery's own scope, as Cqrs's `INotificationDelivery`, which Messaging.Wolverine's scoped internal `NotificationDelivery` implements and `DeliverHandler` alone sets; the Integration Event publisher and the realtime publisher read it (the reviews' F1 and F8; ADR 0012). `RealtimeTests.A_trusted_peers_command_and_a_command_continued_through_the_gateway_cannot_push`: a trusted peer's HTTP command and a command the Stub's Gateway runs with `Continue()`, each a trusted continuation in a Unit of Work, are refused with the publisher's message. `RealtimeTests.A_command_a_notification_handler_sends_through_the_gateway_with_its_own_context_cannot_push_or_publish`: a Notification Handler sends a command through the Stub's Gateway with its delivery's injected context, then fails; the command's push and its Integration Event, published with the delivered Domain Event's identity, are both refused with the publishers' messages, the client's next event is a later push, and no Integration Event of the note arrives | Red once with the push let through for any trusted continuation in a Unit of Work: both pushed. Red once against the first fix round's `OperationContext.Notification`: the relayed command's push and Integration Event were both accepted, `Actual: Tuple (null, null)` |

## gRPC, ticket #134

Ticket #134 of spec #115: `PouryaKit.Grpc`, on `PouryaKit.Web`, `Grpc.AspNetCore.Server` and `Grpc.Net.ClientFactory` 2.84.0. A Module declares a gRPC service with `AddPouryaKitGrpcService<T>()`; the Host maps every one with `MapPouryaKitGrpcServices()` on a root group that requires authorization and carries Web's `BeginOperationPerRequest()` (#119); `ToGrpcResponse` answers a failed `Result` as a status by G1 with every Error in the `pouryakit-errors-bin` trailer; `AddPouryaKitGrpcClient<T>(name)` registers a client whose interceptor writes the context each call is given with `WithOperationContext` through `OperationContextHttpHeaders.Pairs`, with its address and deadline from `PouryaKitGrpcClientOptions`, validated at start; `GrpcLoopbackCheck` fails the start of a Host whose client is addressed at one of its own listening URLs. Catalog's `ProductGrpcService` answers `GetProduct` from `products.proto` in `Catalog.Contracts`. `GrpcTests` runs two Hosts of the application in one test process, each with a client of the other's in-memory server. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium headless.

## Batch 3 follow-ups, ticket #158

Ticket #158 of spec #115: four defects a Codex review of PR #143 found in `PouryaKit.Storage.AzureBlob` (#128) and `PouryaKit.Grpc` (#134), each a small fix inside its package, with no new dependency and no change to `IFileStorage`, Web or the gRPC public API. Kestrel's default listener is the one its current endpoint documentation states for .NET 8 and later ("If there's no endpoint configuration, Kestrel binds to the `http://localhost:5000` URL") and ASP.NET Core 10.0.13's `AddressBinder.DefaultAddressStrategy` binds: `http://localhost:5000` only. The `https://localhost:5001` the ticket names was ASP.NET Core 6's default, with a development certificate; a launch profile's `applicationUrl` reaches the Host as `urls`, which the check already reads.

|---|---|---|
| A malformed account key in the service-URL form fails the Host's start naming the option; a valid one still starts | `AddPouryaKitAzureBlobStorage` validates a non-blank `AccountKey` by building the `StorageSharedKeyCredential` the provider signs with, which decodes it as base64, as `SignsLinks` parses a connection string. `AzureBlobStorageTests.A_host_whose_account_key_is_not_base64_fails_to_start_naming_the_option`: one failure, `PouryaKitAzureBlobStorageOptions.AccountKey is not a base64 account key.`; `AzureBlobStorageTests.A_host_bound_to_the_service_url_and_account_key_stores_a_file_and_signs_its_link` still starts with Azurite's key; `A_host_with_invalid_storage_options_fails_to_start_naming_each_problem` keeps its five messages | Red once with the key rule always true: the Host started |
| A client at `http://localhost:5000` in a Host with no configured listener fails the start; the explicit-listener cases stay green | `GrpcLoopbackCheck` takes `http://localhost:5000` as the listening URL when `app.Urls`, `urls`, `http_ports`, `https_ports` and `Kestrel:Endpoints` give none, after the precedence, so `preferHostingUrls` is unaffected. `GrpcTests.A_client_addressed_at_kestrels_default_url_in_a_kestrel_host_with_no_listener_fails_the_start` (on Kestrel since the review fix below); the eight explicit-listener rows pass unchanged | Red once with the default dropped: the Host started |

## AI client and the Gateway tool, ticket #135

Ticket #135 of spec #115: the optional `PouryaKit.AI`, referencing `PouryaKit.Cqrs` and `PouryaKit.Modularity`, as the spec's AI decision places it, with its decisions A1 (one chat client for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and Ollama through the `OpenAI` client, no `OllamaSharp`) and A2 (the guarantees against an in-process OpenAI-compatible stub, one opt-in probe against Ollama). `AddPouryaKitAI()` builds the Host's one `IChatClient` from `PouryaKitAIOptions`, validated at start; `Tool` on a Module's `IGatewayProcessor<TModule>` makes a command or query a Gateway tool. The Proving Sample's agent is Catalog's `AskAboutProductsQueryHandler`, whose run gives the model `GetProduct` through Catalog's Gateway, as the asking Actor. `AiTests` runs the application on a database of its own with its chat client pointed at `ChatStub`, a chat completions server in the test process on a loopback port. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.11.0, OpenAI 2.14.0.

## Agent runs, ticket #136

Ticket #136 of spec #115: the rest of plan I.4's AI design in `PouryaKit.AI`, on the Microsoft Agent Framework (`Microsoft.Agents.AI` and `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Workflows` 1.25.0), as the owner's 2026-10-06 answer 3 decided. An agent, `AsAIAgent` over the Host's one `IChatClient`, keeps that client's function invocation and adds none, so the allow-list, the cap and the guardrails hold for each run and each agent of a workflow. The Kit adds `IChatGuardrail` and its step inside function invocation, the port `IAgentSessionStore` (`FindAsync`, `SaveAsync`) and the agent's `LoadSessionAsync` and `SaveSessionAsync` over it, and a declaration rule in the allow-list; reducers, memory and workflows are the framework's, as it ships them. `AgentRunTests` runs on a database of its own with the chat client pointed at `ChatStub`, which now streams when a request asks it to and can answer each request from its body. Each run that calls a tool executes inside an authorized Operation, through the test Module's `RunAgentQuery`, and each `GetProduct` call's context is asserted as `AiTests` asserts it: the run's Actor, tenant and correlation, the run's Operation id as causation, an Operation id of its own, no request id, a trusted continuation. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.11.0, Microsoft.Agents.AI 1.25.0.

## MCP client, ticket #137

Ticket #137 of spec #115, user story 54 (MCP): the Host's clients of the MCP servers `PouryaKitAIOptions.McpServers` names, over stdio or HTTP, in `PouryaKit.AI` on the official MCP C# SDK's client package, `ModelContextProtocol.Core` 2.2.0 (Apache-2.0). `IMcpServers`, a singleton of the Host's services, connects each server at its first listing and is disposed with those services, so no run owns a client; its tools, the SDK's `McpClientTool`s, are functions a run is given beside its Gateway tools, so the Host's one `ToolAllowList` and one iteration cap hold for them with no change to either. Against the in-process `ChatStub`, a stdio server that is the test assembly `ModularMonolith.Tests.McpServer` started with `dotnet`, and an HTTP server in the test process: no network and no hosted key.

## Embeddings and pgvector, ticket #138

Ticket #138 of spec #115: embeddings for the three providers in `PouryaKit.AI` and semantic search over pgvector in the new `PouryaKit.AI.Postgres`, in the package's own schema, so a Host without it takes no pgvector (spec #115's AI decision, plan I.4, user story 55). `AddPouryaKitEmbeddings()` builds the Host's `IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>` on the chat client's one OpenAI client from the same `PouryaKitAIOptions`, its `EmbeddingModel` validated at start. `AddPouryaKitVectorStore()` gives a Module `IVectorStore`, which stores text by its embedding on the Unit of Work's transaction and searches by cosine distance, both within the Operation's tenant, in tables `ai.<collection>` that the migration helper `CreateVectorCollection` creates with the `vector` extension. `CommunityToolkit.VectorData.PgVector` 1.0.1, which plan I.4 names, is MIT and targets .NET 10, and is not used: its collection writes on a connection of its own, outside the Unit of Work (ADR 0003); nor is the `Pgvector` client, since an embedding goes as a `real[]` that pgvector casts ([provenance](provenance/PouryaKit.AI.Postgres.md)).

## Ollama in the AppHost, ticket #139

Ticket #139 of spec #115: `AddPouryaKitOllama(name, model)` in `PouryaKit.Aspire`, and the Proving Sample's `ModularMonolith.AppHost` running Catalog's agent against it. The registration is a plain container on `docker.io/ollama/ollama:0.40.6`, the image of `AiTests`' Ollama probe, with an HTTP endpoint on port 11434 and a named volume at `/root/.ollama`; the toolkit package the plan's I.3 row names, `CommunityToolkit.Aspire.Hosting.Ollama` 13.6.0, brings `OllamaSharp` 5.4.12, whose licence is a file (spec #115's A1), so it is not used. Its health check, the internal `OllamaModelHealthCheck`, is healthy only once the server has the model, which it pulls into the volume, so `WaitFor` starts a Host with its model served. The sample AppHost adds it only with `LocalAgent=true` and sets `ModularMonolith.Host`'s `PouryaKit__AI__Provider`, `__Endpoint` (the endpoint with `/v1`) and `__Model`; Catalog's new `POST /catalog/v2/products/ask` (or the unversioned path with the `api-version` header) sends a caller's question to the agent. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, Aspire 13.6.1.

## Report Module, ticket #140

Ticket #140 of spec #115, user stories 63 to 67: `PouryaKit.Reporting.Module`, the first Module the Kit ships as a package (E2), which the Proving Sample's Host adds once with `modules.Add<ReportModule>()` beside its own Modules, with its one report kind, `SalesReports`, implementing the two ports (E3: `IReportRequestAuthorizer` and `IReportLayouts`) and an S3 bucket as its file storage. It references Modularity, Persistence.Postgres, Persistence.Dapper, Messaging.Wolverine.EFCore, Validation, Security, Web, Reporting and Storage, its own schema `reports`, and is not tenant-scoped: it stores each job's tenant as a column and enforces ownership itself. The proof is `ReportModuleTests` over HTTP, on a database of its own beside `AppFixture`'s PostgreSQL 18.6 and a RustFS 1.0.2 bucket (`ReportFixture`). Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, Archify 3.0.1 with Playwright's Chromium headless.

| Criterion | Test or change | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A request answers 202 and a job id; an unauthorized request creates no job and no scheduled delivery | `A_request_answers_202_with_the_job_whose_file_the_background_renders_and_stores_for_its_requester`: `POST /reports` answers 202 with `{ id }` and `Location: /reports/{id}`. `A_request_the_hosts_port_refuses_answers_403_and_stores_no_job_and_schedules_nothing`: the sample's `SalesReports` refuses a month that does not parse; the answer is 403 `Reports.RequestDenied`, no job row holds the request, and the message store holds no new claim | Red once with the authorizer's answer ignored: 202 instead of 403 |
| The background job renders through the renderer, stores through the storage contract and reports the location; another Actor's and another tenant's reads answer not found and mint no URL | The first test follows the job to `Completed` over `GET /reports/{id}`, downloads its file through the presigned link with a plain `HttpClient`, and compares it with `ReportRenderer`'s CSV of the sample's layout; the Host's layout was asked for under a trusted continuation of the request, its Actor, tenant and correlation. `Only_the_requester_within_the_jobs_tenant_or_an_actor_granted_the_tenants_jobs_reads_it_and_no_one_else_gets_a_link`: another Actor of the tenant, the requester under another tenant and an Actor granted `reports.jobs.read-tenant` in another tenant each get 404 `Reports.JobNotFound`, and `RecordingFileStorage`, in front of the S3 provider, signed no link for any of them; an Actor granted `reports.jobs.read-tenant` in the job's tenant reads it with its link, as spec #115's Reporting decision has it: "a tenant-wide read is a permission the Host grants" | Red once each: the claim scheduled a year out (the job stayed `Requested`); the requester check off (200 for another Actor); the tenant predicate off (200 under another tenant); a link signed before the checks (one more signed key) |
| A stale claim is taken over once, a late settlement is refused, and the bytes downloaded afterwards are the winning attempt's | `A_stale_claim_is_taken_over_once_its_late_settlement_is_refused_and_the_winning_attempts_file_is_served`: the test Host's `TestReports` holds the first layout of its `held` kind past the 2 s claim timeout; the one takeover claims attempt 2, which renders and settles; released, attempt 1 stores its file under `reports/{id}/1` and its settlement is refused by the job's version; retried, it finds the claim taken and deletes that file (since the review fix round). The job serves `reports/{id}/2`, whose bytes the link downloads; the message store holds the job's claims of attempts 1 and 2 alone, read from their envelopes; the layout was asked for twice | Red once each: one key for every attempt (the download read attempt 1's bytes); the settlement unfenced, the attempt check off (attempt 1 settled after its retry re-rendered); a takeover scheduled by every claim (claims `[1, 2, 2]`) |
| Retention removes expired output across tenants and never a published object | `Retention_removes_the_expired_jobs_and_files_of_every_tenant_and_never_a_file_a_job_serves`: three completed jobs, two of them in two tenants moved past their expiry; the retention, a recurring command of the system Actor `reports.retention` every second in the test Host, expires them, and a later occurrence deletes their files and the jobs: both files are gone from the store, the first job answers 404, and the third job still downloads its file | Red once each: the retention reading only jobs with no tenant (the expired jobs stayed); the expiry check off (the served job's file was deleted) |
| The Module is a Module like any other under the structure tests | `Sample.Modules` takes the package up as the sample Host's fifth Module, beside Ledger: `ModuleBoundaryTests` (no reference to another Module, public types its Composition Root and the two ports with `ReportRequest`, listed in `HostPorts`), `FeatureCodeTests` (no save, commit or transport type, its DbContext the fourth model mapping no envelope), `NamespaceTests` (one namespace, ADR 0010) and `PackageGraphTests` (its row; a storage provider or SDK in its closure refused) | The structure tests pass with the package among the Modules; `PackageGraphTests.A_closure_with_a_package_section_c_keeps_out_is_rejected` refuses `AWSSDK.Core` and `PouryaKit.Storage.S3` in its closure |
| Design choices | Each claim commits on its own before its attempt renders, so the takeover sees it; the attempt number and the aggregate's `Version` fence every claim, settlement and expiry; the first claim schedules the one takeover, and a takeover schedules none. Generation is two delayed commands, `reports.claim` and `reports.render`, continuations of the request. The job read is Dapper's, within the lease's tenant. A tenant-wide read is the permission `reports.jobs.read-tenant` the Host's `IActorPermissions` grants. Retention expires first and deletes a job's files in a later occurrence, once the expiry is committed. The Module binds its settings, internal, from `PouryaKit:Reports`, as a Module binds its own (modules.md), so its only public types are those ADR 0001 allows. The connection string is the Module's constant `app`: a Composition Root receives no configuration | |

## Saga package, ticket #142

Ticket #142 of spec #115, user stories 68 to 72: the optional `PouryaKit.Messaging.Wolverine.Sagas` (Messaging.Wolverine; `WolverineFx.Postgresql` 6.48.3, the Kit's line), built as ADR 0013 records it, its #142 amendment saying where it departs from the Spike's shape. A Module declares a Saga with `AddPouryaKitSaga<TSaga>(name, systemActor, saga => saga.Input<TEvent>(key).Timeout<TTimeout>())` and derives it from `PouryaKitSaga`, its steps taking `SagaInput<TSaga, TEvent>` and its timeouts deriving from `SagaTimeout`. The proof is `SagaTests` in `ModularMonolith.Tests`, over the test Modules `tests/ModularMonolith.Tests/Sagas` (Orders publishes, Billing is tenant-scoped and subscribes, Shipping runs the Sagas) and their Host `ModularMonolith.Tests.Sagas.Host`, each test on a database of its own in the broker collection's PostgreSQL 18.6, the crash cases in the child process `ModularMonolith.Tests.SagaChild`, the fan-out with two Hosts on the collection's RabbitMQ. Each deciding test was run once with its behaviour switched off, by a one-line mutation, and failed. The Proving Sample declares no saga: the spec names none. Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402, Docker 29.8.2, WolverineFx 6.48.3.

## Batch 5 follow-ups, ticket #159

Ticket #159 of spec #115: four defects a Codex review of PR #143 found in `PouryaKit.Realtime` (#133) and `PouryaKit.Grpc` (#134, #158), each a focused fix with no new package and no public API change beyond an XML summary. ASP.NET Core 10.0.13's Kestrel exposes no public reading of the listeners `ConfigureKestrel` sets in code (`KestrelServerOptions.CodeBackedListenOptions`, `OptionsInUse` and `GetListenOptions()` are internal), so the loopback check compares a second time once the server has bound, as the ticket's fallback says. macOS ControlCenter (AirPlay Receiver) holds `*:5000` on the machine these runs used, so no test binds Kestrel's default port: the default is proven by its comparison over a bound-address list.

| Criterion | Test or change | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A Domain Event Handler running in a Notification Handler's delivery cannot push or publish; the Notification Handler still can | `DeliverHandler` sets `NotificationDelivery.Notification` before `Subscription.InvokeAsync` and clears it in a `finally`, before the Unit of Work drains the Domain Events the handler raised in that scope (ADR 0012's amendment). `RealtimeTests.A_domain_event_handler_of_a_notification_handlers_change_cannot_push_or_publish_while_the_handler_can`: the Stub's `PushThenWriteNoteNotificationHandler` pushes, then writes a note raising a Domain Event whose `PushAndShareWrittenNoteReaction` tries both publishers; both refuse with their messages, the client's events are the handler's push and then a later one, and no Integration Event of the note arrives. `RealtimeTests` and `NotificationTests` green | Red once with the record left set: `Actual: Tuple (null, null)` |
| A `TimeSpan.MaxValue` deadline sends the call with no deadline | The one rule: a call without a deadline of its own gets the client's, or `DateTime.MaxValue`, which gRPC sends as none, when the client's would end after it (`OperationContextInterceptor`; `PouryaKitGrpcClientOptions.Deadline`'s summary and `grpc.md`). `GrpcTests.A_client_whose_deadline_ends_after_the_latest_time_sends_its_call_with_no_deadline`: the call answers, and its request carries no `grpc-timeout` | Red once with the cap off: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `DateTime.op_Addition` in the interceptor |
| A client at a code-configured listener's address fails the start, and a client at port 5000 beside such a listener starts; the explicit-listener cases stay green | `GrpcLoopbackCheck` keeps its configured-address comparison before any hosted service starts, without the default, and, as an `IHostedLifecycleService` registered beside it, compares in `StartedAsync`, only where the server is Kestrel, the addresses `IServerAddressesFeature` lists once Kestrel has bound: listeners set in code, a port 0 and the default; its message adds that the Host had already bound them. `GrpcTests.A_client_addressed_at_a_listener_kestrel_binds_from_code_stops_the_host_and_fails_its_start` (`ListenLocalhost` on a free port, the client there, the exact message); `GrpcTests.A_client_addressed_at_kestrels_default_url_starts_beside_a_listener_kestrel_binds_from_code`; `GrpcTests.Kestrels_default_among_the_bound_addresses_refuses_a_client_there_and_no_other` (the comparison over `http://localhost:5000`, refusing `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` there and admitting port 5001). The eight explicit-listener rows, the Kestrel Host listening elsewhere and the Host without a server pass unchanged; #158's `A_client_addressed_at_kestrels_default_url_in_a_kestrel_host_with_no_listener_fails_the_start` is removed, since it would bind port 5000 (`check-docs.py`'s `REMOVED_TESTS`) | Red once with the bound comparison off: the code listener's Host started. Red once with #158's pre-bind default restored: the Host beside the code listener failed, naming `http://localhost:5000` |
| A blank or whitespace `channel` value is 400 `ChannelRequired`; the admitted-channel cases stay green | `MapPouryaKitRealtime` answers `RealtimeErrors.ChannelRequired` when any named value is blank or whitespace, before the endpoint's rule runs. `RealtimeTests.A_request_naming_a_blank_channel_is_refused_as_naming_none`: `?channel=`, `?channel=%20` and `?channel=stub.notes&channel=` are each 400 `Realtime.ChannelRequired`; `RealtimeTests.A_client_listens_only_on_the_channels_the_endpoint_admits_for_its_actor` stays green | Red once with the blank arm off: 403 `Forbidden` for each row |
| `realtime.md`, `grpc.md`, ADR 0012 and the XML summaries say what the code does | The skill's [realtime.md](../.agents/skills/pourya-kit/references/realtime.md) (the delivery's own Domain Event Handlers, the blank Channel) and [grpc.md](../.agents/skills/pourya-kit/references/grpc.md) (the deadline rule, the loopback rule's two comparisons); [ADR 0012](adr/0012-realtime-through-postgresql-notifications.md)'s dated amendment; [`docs/architecture/README.md`](architecture/README.md)'s Realtime paragraph, publisher and gRPC bullets; the summaries of `GrpcLoopbackCheck`, `AddPouryaKitGrpcClient`, `PouryaKitGrpcClientOptions.Deadline`, `MapPouryaKitRealtime` and `RealtimeErrors.ChannelRequired` | `check-docs.py` and `check-ai-setup.py`: 0 failures |

## Wave 4 The AppHost's Reverse proxy and service route, ticket #170

Ticket #170 of spec #161 (spec ticket 7's AppHost sentences, user stories 19 and 20, owner decisions W4 and W11). The sample AppHost adds `ModularMonolith.ReverseProxy` as the project resource `reverse-proxy`, which references and waits for both Hosts and has its own `/alive` health check, and gives it the service route through its environment: `/inventory/{**catch-all}` to the cluster `inventory`, destination `http://inventory`, active probe `true`. The proxy's own `appsettings.json` keeps routing every path to `ModularMonolith.Host` with that cluster's probe off (W11). The route is the AppHost's, not the settings', because only beside a broker does Inventory run in `Inventory.Host`: without one `ModularMonolith.Host` hosts Inventory and serves its paths, which the settings' catch-all sends it when the proxy runs alone. The proxy's listening URL moved from its `appsettings.json` (`Urls`) to `Properties/launchSettings.json`: the first start test showed `Now listening on: http://localhost:5100` and `Resource 'reverse-proxy' failed to become healthy` after five minutes, since `Urls` from `appsettings.json` overrides the `ASPNETCORE_URLS` Aspire passes. #169 had already given `inventory` the bearer environment. No Kit package, template or `ModularMonolith.Host` change; no new package.

## Wave 4 the service template, ticket #171

Ticket #171 of spec #161 (spec ticket 8, owner decisions W3 and W4, user stories 9, 10 and 15 to 18). `dotnet new pouryakit-service` generates the third composition: Inventory, packed from the Proving Sample as the other templates pack their Modules, with Catalog's Contracts, a Host composed as `Inventory.Host` is (the service defaults and Serilog, JWT bearer with the `tenant` claim, the Web defaults, the API versions and OpenAPI, `AddPouryaKitModules` with `InventoryModule`, `Receive` and `ReceiveSnapshot` of Catalog's three wire names, Observability, Wolverine over EF Core, RabbitMQ always under the derived service name), its own `https` launch profile on 7081 and 5081, `WolverineFx.RuntimeCompilation` in Debug builds only, `RunJasperFxCommands`, and a test project whose `App`, a `HostFixture` of `PouryaKit.Testing`, starts RabbitMQ (`Testcontainers.RabbitMq`, already a root pin) before the fixture starts PostgreSQL and the Host, by implementing `IAsyncLifetime` again over the fixture's own. Inventory's project file moved from `content/modular` to `content/shared`; the monolith's source of the shared content excludes it, and the service's sources take only the ServiceDefaults, `Catalog.Contracts` and Inventory from the shared content and the sample. No AppHost in any template (W4), no Kit library and no `validate.py` change: the inventory row is the whole validation change. ## Wave 4 the polished sample agent, ticket #173

Ticket #173 of spec #161 (spec ticket 10, owner decisions W6 and W6b, user stories 25 to 31, 33 and 34). Catalog's `AskAboutProducts` is now a command, since a query cannot write (ADR 0003): `AskAboutProductsCommandHandler` runs an Agent Framework agent over the Host's one chat client with the `GetProduct` Gateway tool, its history bounded by `MessageCountingChatReducer(20)`, in the asking Actor's conversation in the tenant. The conversation is one aggregate of Catalog's, `ProductConversation` (`catalog.product_conversations`, a Guid key and a unique index on the conversation's key, migration `ProductConversations`), plain EF code packed into both templates, keyed by a Guid version 7 as the Kit's tenant rule for a Snapshot's identity asks of a tenant-scoped Module's aggregates (`CompositionCheckTests.A_snapshot_in_a_tenant_scoped_module_is_judged_by_the_aggregates_of_its_own_db_context_only` publishes every aggregate of Catalog's DbContext, and refused a string key); `ProductConversations` implements `IAgentSessionStore` over it through the repository, and the memory, `ProductsAskedAbout`, an `AIContextProvider`, keeps the products `GetProduct` found in the same row, so the command's Unit of Work writes the session and the memory, or neither. A turn the Host's guardrail refuses fails with `Product.QuestionRefused`: a refused question kept in the session would be sent, and refused, again with every later turn. The Host registers the application's guardrail, `CardNumberGuardrail`, which `PouryaKit.Templates` packs from the sample for the modular template's Host. No Kit package changed, no package was added, and there is no semantic search and no pgvector (W6b). Environment: macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.402.

## Wave 4 One embedding generator per Host, ticket #174

Ticket #174 of spec #161 (spec ticket 11, owner decision W6c, user story 32), the Wave's one Kit API change. `AddPouryaKitEmbeddings` registers Cqrs's `OneProviderCheck<IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>>("AddPouryaKitEmbeddings", "embedding generator")` with `TryAddEnumerable`, as `AddPouryaKitAI` registers the chat client's: the rule that a guarantee the final registrations can answer is a build-time composition check now covers the generator, and the AI reference's "one embedding model per Host" limit, which nothing enforced (#138), became a guarantee. No new check type. By the session's scope grant, `OneProviderCheck` names a generic contract with its type arguments in angle brackets, `IEmbeddingGenerator<String, Embedding<Single>>`, instead of its CLR name with a backtick and its arity; the non-generic contracts' messages are unchanged. ## Wave 4 close-out, ticket #176

Ticket #176 of spec #161, criterion 1's fix round: the whole-branch close-out reviews of PR #177 (`8e69b777..29c0fb41`) returned no high, five mediums and eight lows, every one verified against the code before this round; each is fixed below with its check. The README status sentence and the plan's three status clauses say Wave 4 is complete on `wave-4`. The fixes are commit `7494a9d2` on `29c0fb41`.

| Behaviour | Proof | Check result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 (Codex F1, shard B1): the Docker waiter counts a process by what it runs, a Python running `scripts/packaging/validate.py`, `dotnet test` or a VSTest host, read from `ps -Ao command=`, so a shell that chains the waiter with its command (`sh -c "wait-docker-quiet.sh && …"`) no longer blocks another waiter | `.agents/scripts/wait-docker-quiet.sh`; a run on `4cd16683`'s waiter, with the base's waiter as the red case: `python3 <scratchpad>/p176/proof176.py <base waiter> .agents/scripts/wait-docker-quiet.sh <fake>/scripts/packaging/validate.py`, where the fake validation sleeps its first argument's seconds. Each case starts the fake for 20 s, then two waiters a second apart, `sh -c "<waiter> 1 && python3 <fake> 10 W<n>-command"` | Base waiter: the fake ended at 10:19:51; W1 printed `still busy after 1 minutes` and exited 2 at 10:20:32, and W2 ran only once W1's waiting shell was gone, at 10:20:33. This ticket's waiter: the fake ended at 10:21:03; W1's command ran 10:21:15 to 10:21:25 and W2's, which waited for W1's command, a validation itself, 10:21:46 to 10:21:56; both exited 0 |
| M1 (Codex F1; fix round 2, N1 and N2): a waiter given a command, `wait-docker-quiet.sh [max-minutes] -- <command>`, takes the machine's lock directory `/tmp/pourya-kit-docker.lock`, holding its PID, as soon as no other waiter holds it, waits while holding it until Docker is quiet, runs the command and exits with the command's status; without a command it only waits, for a quiet Docker and a free lock. A stale lock, whose holder no longer runs (`ps -p`, which sees another user's PID where `kill -0` fails with EPERM) or which holds no PID and is more than a minute old, is reclaimed by renaming it to a name of the reclaimer's own, which only one waiter can do, and removed only if the renamed directory still holds the PID judged dead; a lock taken again in between is put back, and a taker reads its PID back before it counts the lock. The brief template, `AGENTS.md`, the AI-setup guide and `running-a-spec.md` run the full suite and `validate.py` through it | `WaitDockerQuietTests.test_a_lock_whose_holder_is_gone_is_reclaimed_and_a_running_holders_kept` (a gone PID, the test's own, PID 1), `WaitDockerQuietTests.test_a_lock_without_a_pid_is_being_taken_for_a_minute_then_reclaimed` and `WaitDockerQuietTests.test_a_reclaimer_that_judged_an_older_holder_dead_leaves_the_lock_taken_since`, the script's functions sourced with the lock in a temporary directory, 0.1 s. The same run: two waiters `sh -c "<waiter> 2 -- sh <scratchpad>/p176/job.sh 10 W<n>-command"`, a command no Docker-user pattern matches, behind the 20 s fake; a lock holding PID 99999 and `<waiter> 1 -- sh -c 'echo command runs; exit 3'`; `<waiter> 0 -- …` against a fresh lock without a PID, a lock of PID 1 and a lock without a PID two minutes old; three rounds of two waiters started together on a lock whose holder had exited, each running `job.sh 5` | Red once each with a rule switched off: reclaiming in place without the check, liveness through `kill -0` (PID 1 read as dead) and a PID-less lock never stale each failed their test. The rename's atomicity is reasoned, not raced: the renamed directory's name is the reclaimer's own, which no other waiter touches. The run: the fake ended at 10:22:16; W1's command ran 10:22:27 to 10:22:37 and W2's, held by the lock alone, 10:22:58 to 10:23:08, both exit 0. The stale lock was taken at once, the waiter exited 3 and left no lock. Cap 0: the fresh lock and PID 1's exited 2, `still busy`; the old one was reclaimed and its command ran. The races: in each, one command ran at once (10:23:08, 10:23:44, 10:24:19) and the other 30 s later, after the first had ended (10:23:38, 10:24:14, 10:24:49), every waiter exited 0 and no lock or renamed directory was left.
